Metrics keep every value but fold to two columns, 2x2 or 2x3, in one panel with a 1px rule between columns and no boxes. Three across works if labels fit 110px. Numbers 20 to 28px tabular. Charts keep their axes at 280 to 300px tall.

A filter sidebar collapses to one control: a 36 to 50px icon chip, one open-filters button beside sort, or a two-column list of bare heads. Results move up so the first thumbnail shows on screen one. Keep the active filter count visible.

A wide compare table shows one plan at a time: name, price and a full-width button flanked by 36px previous and next arrows, pinned on scroll. Feature groups collapse, rows 53px, single column. No sideways scroll and no squeezed columns.

Plans stack one per screen at 16 to 24px gutters, 8 to 24px gaps, CTA full width in each card, billing toggle centred above and pinned if long. Collapse the free plan to one row, name left and price right, so the paid plan arrives sooner.

Plan columns survive as a sideways rail: 250px columns split by hairlines, next plan peeking at the edge, tile, button and list intact. Keeps plans comparable where a stack does not. Shorten tab labels to fit. Best with three to five plans and short lists.

Rank the columns. Keep the name and one key value, and move the rest to a 13px second line inside the name cell, or drop them. Never scroll the whole table. Rows 56 to 64px tall, tabular figures, right-aligned value, 1px rules.

Code never wraps and never shrinks under 13px. Keep 13 to 15px mono, line numbers and filename tab, and clip at the card edge or run the card off the right, with overflow-x auto inside the block. Install commands truncate but keep the copy button.

A long tab strip collapses to one control: a full-width 44 to 48px native select, or a centred label with left and right chevrons. Every option stays reachable and nothing clips. Use a select past four options or for long labels.

Exposed page rails survive by moving out to the gutter: verticals 16 to 24px from each edge, horizontal rules snapping on, nodes kept, cards inset inside them. The rails are the identity, so never drop them for space. For developer and finance pages.

A ruled grid stacks to full-width rows. Horizontal rules stay, vertical rules go, adjacent cells share one border so no line doubles. Labels move above their content, 16 to 24px padding. The grid logic survives with no cards added.

Keep the desktop stagger inside one column: a picture indented 50px, a photo running off one edge with a caption card crossing its corner, or two offset lanes. Insets of 12 to 50px are enough. Beats a centred stack for editorial and brand pages.

Design it as a document and the phone needs almost nothing: same type scale, same chrome, one column, 16 to 24px gutters, no restyle. Body stays 14 to 19px. Best for essays, manifestos, portfolios and strict systems where the voice is the design.

The headline stays huge because it is the design: 17vw sets about 66px on a 390 screen, two to four short lines, tracking -.03em, left or offset. Size it from the longest word and break lines by hand. Only for short phrases.

The wordmark is refit to span the phone, gutter to gutter, about 350px wide, breaking into two rows or stacking letters if needed. Crop an SVG viewBox to the ink so it scales without distortion. Height follows the word. One bold gesture on the first screen.

56 to 64px bar: logo left, one compact action and a menu glyph right, all on one centre line, 16 to 24px gutters. The action is 32 to 40px tall, pill or tile matching the page. Sign-up stays visible and everything else goes behind the menu. Default for products.

Logo and one thin glyph, nothing else: two 18 to 24px hairlines 6 to 8px apart, stroke matching the logo weight, no button shape, 20px margins, no bar fill. Hit area still 44px. Works over photographs and for calm brands.

The menu glyph sits on its own ground: a 36 to 44px square, circle or pill in tint, brand fill or outline, matching the site's button shape. Gives an icon an edge on busy art. A 92 by 46px flush block is the bold form.

No icon: the word Menu set in the site's own link or label style, 13 to 20px, plain or underlined, opposite the mark. Reads as written, not stock. Pad to a 44px hit area. For studios, editorial and type-led sites with no chrome.

Replace the three bars with a glyph from the brand: a descending funnel for a filterable archive, a thin plus, a four-dot grid, lines of unequal length. Same 24px box, same stroke as the logo. One small owned detail beats a redesigned bar.

If three or four links fit at 14 to 16px, show them and drop the menu: a 358px tray spaced evenly, corner links at 16px inset, or inline links under the name. Desktop and phone share one object. Only for sites with under five destinations.

Commerce bar: menu left, mark centred or left, then 20 to 24px line icons for search, account and bag at 44px pitch. A 1fr auto 1fr grid keeps the mark centred whatever each side holds. The count sits in the bag.

A 45px bar split by hairlines into 45px square cells: menu and search left, account and bag right, empty centre until the wordmark docks on scroll. 14 to 16px line icons, no labels. Rigid and fashion-like. A strict grid the rest of the page repeats.

The bar as a floating card: inset 8 to 20px, 56 to 66px tall, radius 16 to 100, white or blurred fill, soft shadow, logo left, menu tile right. The page wash shows in the gutters, so the hero reads as running behind it. Sticky 12px from the top.

The bar stays empty of logo while the hero shows it large. Once scrolled, a 16 to 24px mark docks into the bar, left or centre. Avoids two logos on one screen. Use with a big wordmark hero and a 150 to 200ms fade.

Search is the nav: a 42 to 54px field fills the bar beside a menu icon and account, or stays pinned full width under the header. Links go behind the menu. For marketplaces, directories and catalogues, where people arrive knowing what they want.

For local services: under the logo, a row of actions that do something at once, such as call, email, directions and menu, as 32 to 44px icon buttons with 11px labels, or one split block for Menu and Ask. Real tel and mailto links, not forms.

App-style tabs for sites people use rather than read: three to five icon-and-label items, 24 to 28px icons, 10 to 11px labels, 56 to 64px tall plus safe area, opaque, top hairline or rounded top. One active colour. Never on a marketing page.

The site nav moves to the foot: a 60px bar with mark left and three or four 32px framed icon buttons right, or a darker 40px search strip above a row of 16px links. The top of the page stays free. For docs and developer sites.

A floating dock instead of a bar: a 52px capsule inset 16px from edges and base, name left, one high-contrast Menu pill right, or a 54px menu circle beside a 245px CTA pill, or one 46px button alone. Thumb reach, no top bar needed.

The docs sidebar becomes a 44 to 48px sticky bottom bar: section icon, current section, chevron. A tap raises the same tree as a sheet capped at 60svh, with the current page tinted and a scrim behind. Location stays visible and within thumb reach.

Two stacked sticky rows in docs: a 56px identity row with logo, version, search and overflow, then a 40 to 56px row with menu glyph and breadcrumb ending in the current page. The sidebar hides and the location stays. Truncate the path, never the page name.

A row under the header that scrolls sideways and clips at the screen edge: 11 to 14px links or chips, or 60px round photos with 12px labels, cut through the fifth item. Pin the section name at left. Fade only the right end.

No entrance at all: every word and control is final at first paint, nothing fades or moves. Keep one ambient object running, such as a live counter, a drifting gradient or a film. Reading starts in under 0.5s, so the page feels fast and sure of itself.

Whole page appears in its final position at 25-65% ink and reaches full ink within 0.4-1s, with no translate, stagger or scale. Opacity 0.3-0.4s on cubic-bezier(.25,0,.5,1). Reads like a print developing, and it is the quietest entrance that still marks arrival.

Nav, headline and buttons paint at once; the media slot is already reserved at its exact size. Media fades in by about 1-2s with opacity 0.3s cubic-bezier(0,0,.2,1), no slide, no layout shift. Copy never waits for the heavy asset and never moves.

Reserve the hero with a flat plate sampled from the footage's first frame, at the exact size of the video, with nav and headline already placed on it. Fade the media up over 0.8-1.5s on its ready event, not a timer. No spinner, no shift, so a slow connection still looks designed.

Skeleton copies the final geometry exactly: same tile sizes, radii and caption bars in a flat 4-8% grey, with logo and primary controls live at once. Content swaps in tile by tile by about 2s with no reflow and no shimmer sweep. Best for feeds and catalogues.

Nav is solid from frame one. Headline fades from near zero with 8px blur, line by line, then subhead, then product, each about 1.3s on a gentle cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1), starts 0.2-0.5s apart, no travel. Readable by about 1.9s, done by 3s. Sharp out-curves make this pop.

Headline words resolve left to right from 10px blur through a saturated tint of the accent to sharp ink, about 0.75s each with a 140ms stagger, no translate. Subline follows, media last. Complete by about 2s. Use on headlines of seven words or fewer.

Headline lines or words rise 6-12px and fade with a 60-100ms stagger, cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), 0.6-1.1s, while chip and buttons are already in place. A colour field or gradient blooms after the words land. Small travel is the whole difference from a default fade-up.

Copy and backdrop are present first. By 1-2s the product window rises 12-60px from below the fold edge with a fade, cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), 0.7-1s, covering part of the backdrop. A small detail arrives last, such as a chat prompt or live counter. Conversion UI is never delayed.

Copy is static while the product assembles in 3-5 separate beats over 2-6s: card fades in, phone rises 8px through it, a banner lands last, or a status dot turns amber and an alert appears. Each beat is one thing, so the load plays the product's real job.

Headline and buttons are static from first paint. One owned object performs for 2-4s: a pixel glyph draws along its outline, a signal travels a connector, a wordmark rises behind a roofline. Nothing else moves, so the load feels authored and costs almost nothing to run.

Type and layout are final first. Then only light changes: a render rises from a 25% pastel ghost to full saturation in about 1s, or a glow blooms in a corner over 2-3s, with no slide or scale. The page feels lit rather than loaded.

One word in the headline loops through 3-4 products or audiences every 2-4s while the rest of the line holds. Swap with a short fade, 8px blur or retype, 200-300ms, and animate the width so the line re-centres smoothly. It is the only motion in the hero.

No preloader. The hero runs at once and swaps media in place while type stays locked: split halves change on their own beats about 1s apart, or one interior holds 5s then crossfades over 1.5s. No zoom, pan or parallax. The cut rhythm is the entire effect.

One headline line types character by character at 25-45ms a character with a thin caret, after the rest of the hero is already placed, or as the very last beat. Reserve the full line width first so nothing reflows. It makes the headline the event, so use it once.

Images arrive smaller, denser and rotated about 3-8 degrees, then spread and straighten over 1.5-3s with cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) while headline words rise. Stagger 90-140ms from the centre outward. Best where the product is a collection of objects, and the end state must be a real layout.

Hero photo starts at 24-40px blur over a colour sampled from it and sharpens over 1-2s, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), while copy is already readable or fades in with it. Works like a lens racking, and it makes a slow image load look deliberate.

Flat brand colour fills the screen with one small centred mark, 40-100px, no spinner. Mark fades in within 0.5s, holds about 1s, then the page cuts or crossfades in. Under 1.5s in total. Reads as a hotel or house arriving, and it must appear on first visit only.

A real progress counter set large, 120-180px tabular numerals bottom-left, or 14px between two hairlines. It runs 0 to 100 tied to actual loading, usually 1-2s, while stills or a mark work beside it, then hands straight into the hero. A count that takes 5s is a tax.

The logo does something only this brand would do: a monogram writes itself stroke by stroke, a clock's hands sweep to the real time, a character walks in. 1.5-3s on flat ground, no bar or percent, then dissolve to the page. Spend it on brands with an owned mark.

Wordmark centred on a flat screen holds about 1s, then a single element travels and shrinks into its nav slot over 0.8-1.2s on cubic-bezier(.76,0,.24,1) while the panel behind lifts away. The page is already in place underneath. Use FLIP so one object makes the whole trip.

A film title card: blank ground 0.5s, a huge two-line statement or wordmark at 110-120px holds about 1.5-2s with no movement, then a hard cut or plain swap to the page. No fade, no bar. The confidence comes from the stillness and the cut.

A shape opens the page: a centred ring parts, a thumbnail or video tile grows to full bleed, a white stadium expands into the page sheet. 1-1.5s on cubic-bezier(.76,0,.24,1), clip-path or FLIP rather than width, and the shape must come from the brand.

Letters or a logo resolve through stepped states: glyph swaps settling left to right, or block mosaics halving in size. Use steps(), never a smooth tween, 30-60ms a step, 1-2s in total. Lock the text box first so nothing reflows. Suits technical and mono brands only.

A 4-6s scripted opening that plays before any scroll, like a keynote reveal: a case opens, an x-ray resolves into the render, parts slide together. Camera held, one idea, a skip affordance, and first visit only. Reserve it for launches where the object is the whole page.

Statement of 34-72px starts at 15-20% ink. Each word or character reaches full ink tied to scroll position, never to time, with a soft front 1-2 characters wide or a gradient spread over about 3 lines at reading height. Pace follows the reader. One per page, or one per chapter.

Whole lines or paragraphs wait at 15-60% ink and reach full ink one at a time as they near mid-viewport. Opacity or colour only, no translate, no split. Large type stays perfectly still, which is why it feels calmer than a rise. Use for stat stacks and short statements.

A heading resolves left to right behind a moving front: settled letters solid, a short gradient-coloured band at the front, then blurred pale letters ahead, with a second line waiting blurred below. Tie it to scroll. Body copy stays static. Spend it on one heading per section at most.

Copy enters from 8-12px blur and 30% opacity to sharp as it reaches the viewport, 0.4s cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), with no translate. Softer than a rise, and it fits fashion, agency and premium brands. Keep it to display lines, because blurred small text reads as a rendering bug.

Items fade in where they stand with no offset: opacity 0.5s cubic-bezier(.25,1,.5,1), caught at unequal opacity as they pass. No translate, scale or parallax. The most respectful reveal, and it suits catalogues and documentation where layout must never appear to move under the reader.

A row enters left to right: each item 40-80ms after the last, 8-12px lower, about 0.3-0.5s, cubic-bezier(.25,.1,.3,1) or (.16,1,.3,1). The stagger belongs inside the row, not across the page. Runs once, stays small, and only on peers that should read as a set.

Rows brighten as they reach mid-viewport and dim as they leave, so one item is always in focus and the rest hold at about 35%. Transition 0.3-0.5s on opacity. Works for process lists, CVs and timelines. Keep a readable floor, since dimmed rows must still be legible.

Only small marginal objects move: stickers, cut-outs or line art drift at a different rate from the text, 20-80px over the viewport, and fade in near their heading. Panels and type stay still. CSS scroll timelines are enough. Motion lives in the margins, so reading is never disturbed.

Small mono labels enter as random glyphs resolving left to right, or thumbnails enter as a coarse block mosaic. Stepped, 300-600ms, on labels only, with body copy fading normally. Reads as a data read-out. Never decode anything longer than about four words.

1px lines travel along the page grid as you scroll, branching around headings and ending at nodes, with sections fading in behind them. stroke-dashoffset tied to scroll. It links separate sections into one circuit. Keep lines behind the type and on the grid.

Media does the entrance while text stays still: a video anchored to the right margin grows leftward from about 80% to full width, or a product rises from beneath with its screen state changing. 0.78s cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1). Anchor to one edge so the movement has a direction.

Cards pin under a sticky heading; each new card slides over the last, about 50px lower, widths stepping up (1138, 1260, 1320) so depth reads. Cards are translucent with backdrop-filter blur 22px, so covered copy softens where it passes under. Plain position:sticky, three to five cards.

The most useful pin on the web: plan names, prices and CTAs stick under the nav across thousands of pixels of table, and the section title pins until the next replaces it. Rows pass beneath with a hairline and no shadow. position:sticky only, no scroll listeners.

A slim position cue in the page chrome: a 2-3px top line growing with progress under a chapter nav, a 4px tick riding a rail edge, or a dark pill with a playhead. Active chapter updates per section. Use on long pages only, and replace a sticky header rather than add to one.

Panel pins for one screen per step. A left list activates the next item with a 1px rule and full ink, the rest at 40%; the pinned visual on the right swaps or re-lights to match, others dropping to 10%. Three to five steps, and each must also work as a plain stacked list on a phone.

One full-height frame pins while photographs cross-dissolve at the same framing, with a 12px caption block holding bottom-left. Nothing slides. Chapters change by dissolve rather than by page movement, so a long story reads as a slow film. Three to five stills of matching exposure.

A contained window pins and scales with scroll, about 750px wide to 2x, until it crops at the panel edge and UI text reads huge. Set transform-origin on the focal point, stop the scrub about a quarter early so the end holds, and avoid will-change, which blurs text.

Pinned scene where a small rectangle inside the image scales up to become the next image, about 0.3 viewports per step, three or four steps deep. It reads as falling through pictures. Needs images composed for it, with the next frame's edge exactly on the inner rectangle.

The hero does not scroll away. It pins, then either blurs about 40px and washes pale while centred paragraphs sit over it, or the product scales down to about 30% as the next panel lifts. The image becomes a backdrop instead of leaving, so the first chapter carries into the second.

One logo element travels with scroll from a large hero position to the header, for example 686px to 195px or 30px to 15px, scrubbed. The header stays empty until it arrives, so the brand appears once per screen. Scale with transform and align both ends to the same axis.

Vertical scroll drives a sideways pan across 5-10 items while title and index stay fixed and swap as each item reaches focus. Settle 0.7s cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1). Show the next item's edge at all times. Give it a vertical fallback on phones and never trap the wheel without a way out.

Page background, type, rules and nav interpolate together between sections, for example paper to near-black over about half a viewport, with the CTA staying bright above the shift. No wipe and no edge. The colour change is the transition, so the page acts as one surface.

The section argues by scrub: pinned, a scattered collage of the old way (receipts, forms, emails with dashed links) fades to pale wireframe as the heading swaps and one clean window remains. Or a scene flips to wireframe for a data chapter. Motion carries the claim itself.

One pinned 3D subject or layered diagram is scrubbed apart: lid, board and base separate about 250px along dotted guides, or panes fan in perspective. Ground steps tone between chapters, and only copy and the object change. Prerender frames or use a real model. Worth it only for a physical product.

A 1-1.5px line runs down the page and draws with scroll: ahead of the reader it sits at 20% opacity, the drawn portion at full ink. Rounded 20px elbows, nodes at each stop. It passes over type and illustration, and turns the whole page into one route.

One object stays on screen across several sections and changes as you scroll: a mark rotates 20 then 45 degrees, a phone swaps its screen, a model re-skins per project. Copy passes beside it. One object carries the story, so sections stop restarting.

Scroll or arrow keys fly a real camera between scenes in WebGL, with a tick ruler sliding under a fixed needle and a progress count such as 00/08. Needs a fixed-height page, keyboard control and a static fallback. Reserve it for portfolios and launch pages with no conversion job.

Layering links two sections with no fade: a large heading holds still while a 400-580px video card scrolls across it, lifted by one wide shadow, about 0 24px 60px at 20%. Keep the fixed layer legible when covered, and let the top layer exit under the nav.

Replace a hard section edge with a 100-180px band of 12px tiles on a 1px grid, ramping dark through grey to light, top rows randomly missing. Reverse it at the far end of the section. Static or scrubbed, it costs nothing, and the page gets an owned seam.

Wheel input drives a stage instead of the page: the first input fills a CTA and shows a 12px hint, a photo scales 1.08 while letters bend along a curve, or a sentence flies along a path. One screen tall, with visible progress and every key working. Expressive sites only.

Every control moves one step on its own scale: fill changes about 10 L*, dark fills lighten, light and mid fills darken. background-color only, 0.15s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1), no transform, no shadow. The default of Vercel, Grafana and Exa. It reads as a system, not an effect.

Nav items and rows gain a pill of 4-8% ink with the text stepping to full ink, 0.1-0.2s, no movement. On photos or dark grounds use white at 8-20% instead. The chip fills a target the eye can land on, without inventing any new colour.

The control recedes: opacity or alpha falls to 0.75-0.9 on buttons and 0.5-0.7 on links, 0.1-0.2s, with nothing else changing. One rule for every colour, so a page with many brand fills needs no hover palette. Polar and Nuxt run whole systems on it.

The button dims to opacity 0.6 and a hidden arrow stem fades from 0 to 1 beside its chevron, 0.15s cubic-bezier(.215,.61,.355,1), with the fill unchanged. A chevron extending into an arrow says go without moving the box. Stripe's signature, and it needs an SVG with a separate stem path.

On dark UI text, border and surface all step up together, one notch each: grey text to white, border +10 levels, surface +5 to +7, 0.1-0.2s. Never darken on dark, and use no shadow. Linear uses filter brightness(1.03) on cards and brightness(1.3) on links.

The fill jumps to a second brand colour instead of a shade: accent to ink, or black to a pale mint with a dark label. 0.15-0.3s. Border and label move with it. This is loud, so keep it to the one or two actions that matter and give the rest a quieter hover.

Fill and label swap exactly, and the outline button fills: white on ink becomes ink on white. 0.15-0.3s on colour, background and border together. Binary and flat, no lift. Best in mono or two-colour systems, where a third tone would break the logic.

Zero transition on purpose: colour, fill or underline change in one frame. A hard cut reads as fast and printed, like a switch. It suits type-led, editorial and brutalist sites, and it needs one sharp value change, because a 3% tone step with no easing just looks broken.

Links answer with an underline and nothing else: 1px, offset 2-4px, usually in 0s. A drawn version scales from scaleX(0) to 1 in 0.3s cubic-bezier(0,0,.2,1), origin left on enter and right on leave. Keep it on words, because that is the oldest signal the web has.

The page rests in neutrals and every control resolves to one accent on hover: links, titles and rows go ink to accent in 0.15s, and the main CTA fills. The accent appears only under the pointer, so the colour feels earned and the system needs no extra tokens.

Only the arrow moves: +2 to +6px in x, 0.2-0.3s cubic-bezier(.25,1,.5,1), while the fill takes a quiet tone step. Baseten runs it diagonally at (5px,-5px) for up-right arrows. The box stays put, so it gives direction without the page feeling jumpy.

Two stacked labels clipped to one line box, never to the button: the first translates up by its line height, the copy rises from below. 0.32-0.46s cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1). Fill stays unchanged. Precise and mechanical, like a departures board. Hide the copy from screen readers.

A fill layer sweeps in from one side instead of fading: span scaleX 0 to 1 or translateY from just outside the box, 0.3-0.5s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1), label colour following. Set the origin to the entry side so it leaves the way it came. Has a clear direction and a little theatre.

The button rises 1-2px with a two-layer shadow tinted by the brand, alpha about 10% and 16%, 0.2-0.3s cubic-bezier(.25,1,.5,1). Cards lift at most 4px. Measured median lift is 2px on main buttons and 1px on cards, so anything you can clearly see travel is too much.

The button jumps +4px x, -4px y while a solid shadow appears at -4px 4px 0, or a pale plate sits under it and the face moves (-8px,-8px). 0.15s linear or 0.28s cubic-bezier(.215,.61,.355,1). Printed, sticker-like and physical, and it needs a matching system of hard edges.

The button does not move. Its ring thickens from 1px to 2px with box-shadow 0 0 0, and the label steps to full ink, 0.1s ease-in-out. Slack thickens an inset ring over 0.42s. No layout shift, because box-shadow takes no space. Calm, tactile and easy to theme.

Scale only: 1.04-1.05 up on pills, or 0.98 down as a press. 0.15-0.2s, using the scale property so it composes with other transforms. Grows no more than 1-2px on any edge in spirit, and larger buttons take a smaller factor. Consumer and media brands wear it best.

An overshoot curve such as cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1) on something small: a label dot scales 0 to 1 in 0.5s, a logo tilts -8 degrees, a marker slides 4.5px past and back. Keep it under about 200px wide. Playful brands only, because overshoot on a card reads as a toy.

On dark, a soft light replaces movement: box-shadow none to 0 0 32px white at 50%, or 0 6px 16px accent at 12% with the border moving to 40% accent, 0.2s. Inngest fades in a 360px radial spotlight over 0.42s on cards. Spend it on one control, or nothing glows.

The image scales inside a fixed frame with overflow hidden: 1.02-1.05 for product and premium, 1.1 for consumer. Slower than the controls, 0.3-0.6s, and up to 1s on cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1). Apple uses 1.0161. The frame never moves, which is what keeps it dignified.

The card changes what it says rather than how high it sits: a second product image crossfades in over 0.4s, a tinted fill arrives with an underlined line, a typed suffix such as ' > SHOP' appears, or the poster grows 12px. No shadow and no lift.

An inverse highlight: the item under the pointer drops to 35-50% opacity over 0.3-0.4s cubic-bezier(.25,1,.5,1), with no scale or underline. The art keeps its framing, which suits galleries and magazines where the work must not be decorated.

The card stays where it is and only its 1px border darkens one step, for example #EBEBEB to #BDBDBD, 0.12-0.15s. No lift, shadow or scale. Hugging Face adds a faint fill and small corner ticks. It matches a document feel and keeps dense grids calm.

The whole row takes a fill edge to edge in about 0.2s, text following: a pale tint for tables and FAQs, solid ink with cream text for index lists, or text alone turning the accent. Rules and position stay still, and the row must be a single link.

The hovered row does something owned: grows 16px past both table edges with a pale fill and 12px radius, gains a hatched fill and hard offset, shows a 100px gradient segment on its rules, or reveals three thumbnails. 0.2s. Colour and detail appear only under the cursor.

Only the hovered row opens: height grows from about 19-177px to 240-460px, pushing later rows down while the others collapse into strips. 0.5s cubic-bezier(.25,1,.5,1). An index becomes a gallery. Needs a stable pointer path, so give a row no neighbour that jumps under the cursor.

The hovered row snaps to full ink while its neighbours fall to about 30%, and a small thumbnail tile appears in the indent. Use a CSS :has() rule or group hover. Attention moves by subtraction, so the list stays quiet at rest. Polar uses the same idea on menu rows.

A menu trigger's chevron rotates 180 degrees in 0.2-0.3s while the label takes a 5-8% tint. The colour may snap, but the rotation should ease, because the chevron carries the state. Rotate back on close. It is the one transform almost every product nav uses.

Most controls are deliberately inert. Only one kind responds, for example nav links or a single chip, and the hero film or demo holds the attention. Scale AI scales one inner span to 0.9. Across the sample half of cards, rows and text links do nothing at all.

One row of monochrome logos 24-40px high drifts in a centred 760-1200px window, both ends masked to transparent over 40-80px with mask-image. 40-60s per loop, linear. Pause on hover and under reduced motion. It says a long list without a wall of logos.

Logos near each edge blur progressively to unreadable and dim while the centre stays crisp, instead of an opacity mask. Stack three masked backdrop-filter layers at 1, 3 and 8px, with zones sized in percent so a phone keeps its centre. A lens-like focus for dark pages.

The ticker has no fade. It is clipped hard by the page rail or the panel radius, so items appear and vanish exactly at the drawn line. Monochrome logos about 30px high under a closing hairline. Works only where those lines are already the page's structure.

Two rows of 34-44px hairline chips drift in opposite directions inside a 640px window, masked at both ends, second row offset by half a chip. Shows a long integration list in a small space. Add a static line under it naming what the list means.

A full-bleed band 44-120px tall between sections, solid brand colour, 16-52px caps repeating with an owned glyph as separator. Doubles as a hard section seam. Best when the separator is a brand joke: Headspace uses googly eyes whose pupils aim differently in each instance.

One line at 96-145px of bold type runs edge to edge, cropped by both sides, usually the last loud moment before the footer. An asterisk or star separates phrases. Slow it to 30-40s per loop, and let the page's velocity nudge it if you want it to feel alive.

A one-line ticker of real numbers at the hero base: fixed 11px label on the left, scrolling caps labels with tabular values in chips, split by 1px ticks, right edge fading. Values climb live. Proof instead of decoration, and it must use real or honestly labelled data.

Long lists run as texture behind a card or cutout: two to eight rows of 20px text at 20-60% ink, drifting, offset, with a 12px PAUSE MOTION control below. It shows scale without asking anyone to read it. The foreground object must stay fully legible.

Rows of images or video drift across the full width: 224-342px tiles, 16-24px gaps, 60-90s per loop, one to three rows offset, edges washed to the page colour. Include a visible pause control on any video. It softens uneven customer photos into one texture.

A fixed ~44px band at the viewport bottom whose text and fill change with the current slide or section, so it doubles as a progress signal. Or caption-style lines that swap every 3s. It holds state, so it earns its permanent place.

A real DOM card plays a 6-10s script with a drawn cursor: it types in a field, a tick appears, a button presses, a result card slides out. Live UI, not video, so text stays crisp. Animate x and y on separate curves so the path arcs, dip scale on click, hold 2s at the end.

Tabs auto-advance every 5-8s, and a 2-3px line grows along the active tab as a visible timer, then the next takes over. Hover pauses, click takes control and stops the cycle. The timer tells people that the change is deliberate and when it will come.

The hero window types a real prompt or command in bursts, about 40-85ms a character with a 150-240ms beat at each space, then output arrives row by row and older rows dim to 40%. 6-8s per loop, 2s hold on the result. Hover pauses. Proves the claim before any scroll.

Feature cards run small truths in place: figures tick, a bar fills, a checklist advances with spinner then tick, a chart extends and its tag flips. Mono text, loops under 8s. Motion stays inside the UI and the page frame stays still.

The camera does the storytelling: the demo opens zoomed hard into a prompt at about 100px type, then pulls back to the whole builder, or a full window pushes in 3x until one button fills the panel. Attention lands exactly where the claim is. Use for one hero only.

Autoplaying muted clips inside tiles, cutting every 2-3s, with the layout around them still. Use a poster frame, 2-8MB per clip, lazy loading, and a pause control. A synthetic cursor inside the footage performs the action. Cheap to make and easy to keep honest.

The product is drawn as a diagram that runs: packets pass through a band, cards change state at a scan line, or speech flows along a ribbon into a capsule and leaves polished. Confined to one band under the nav, so it never competes with the headline.

Coloured cursors with ~12px name flags drift across a live canvas and act on real objects, while a caret edits a label. Square-cornered tags, three people at most. It shows collaboration as a behaviour, and it makes an empty page feel inhabited.

A small loop drawn in characters or pixels, with no video: an ASCII figure flips between frames, pixels swap on the logo's own grid, a chalk outline jitters between marks. Stepped timing, 6-12 fps. Tiny to ship, and it reads as made by hand.

The control for a loop, drawn small: 2px segments with the current one filling as a timer, a 6px vertical dash stack, or a translucent 110x32 pause pill bottom left. It replaces dots and arrows, and it is also how a looping hero stays accessible.

Over project media a small tag trails the pointer about 15px down-right: 40-94px wide, 10-13px label such as VIEW, lerp about 0.15 per frame. Stays small so the work stays the subject. It replaces the card's button, so the whole tile is the target. Keep the system cursor visible.

Over a rail the pointer gains a 120px flat disc in a pale brand colour with 14px/700 DRAG centred. It is an instruction, so it appears only where the gesture works and scales in from 0.6 in 0.25s. One disc grammar across WATCH and DRAG.

The arrow is replaced with a 12-20px solid dot or square, sometimes flipping colour over dark slabs. No trail, no lag. It costs a little usability, because small targets lose their hotspot. Portfolios only, and leave text fields and all touch devices alone.

A 70-108px object has its own physics rather than following the mouse: scroll throws a solid circle down the viewport and stretches it into a tilted ellipse along velocity, and it recovers round at rest. Never covers controls for long, and it is switched off under reduced motion.

A custom 20-36px arrow or emoji replaces the system cursor, or coloured arrow cursors sit in the page to suggest a live canvas. Trivial to build with the CSS cursor property. Only a very playful brand survives it, and it must fall back to the system cursor.

The page answers the pointer, not the cursor: when it enters a rail the headline blurs about 8px and drops to 20% so the rail takes over, and it returns when focus leaves. Eased over 0.3s. It moves attention, and it needs no custom cursor at all.

A full-screen brand-colour panel wipes across between pages, 0.8-1s on cubic-bezier(.86,0,.07,1), with a centred line or logo at the midpoint. Swap the route while covered. Under 1s in total, and skip it entirely for repeat navigation and under reduced motion.

Name and image are masked by about 10 vertical bars staggering across the width, about 1.4s, cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1). The outgoing title stays legible in the gaps while the next one builds. Rich, precise and tied to product launches. Bars should echo a real edge in the product.

The frame never moves. Title and still cross-swap in the same position, so only image and words change. Duration 0.3-0.6s. The quietest transition that still feels authored, because the layout itself is the constant.

A small outlined toggle reskins the page in a wipe, ground and type changing together while a duplicate nav slides in under the old one. A mood switch in place of a dark-mode toggle. Works as a brand gesture on a portfolio.

Between dark shots the film flips to a near-white, silver, negative-like exposure at about 36%, then returns to black. A shutter flash that separates chapters. It must be fast and rare, and it must respect photosensitivity, so never repeat it within a second.

A solid disc scales on the ground and covers the screen before the next scene appears, about 1s. Use clip-path circle() so it stays crisp. Starts from the click point if it can, because a transition that begins where the person acted feels caused rather than scheduled.

Default product bar: logo, links grouped beside it, actions pushed right. 64 to 68px tall, 14 to 16px links at 400 to 500, each 36px tall with 12px padding, 1px rule at 8 to 10 percent ink. Right: 36px ghost plus solid CTA, radius 6 to 10, gutters on the page rail.

Logo left, links truly centred with a 1fr auto 1fr grid, actions right. 52 to 72px tall, 14 to 16px links, 24 to 40px gaps, tiny 8 to 10px chevrons only on items that open. Bar can match the page colour with no border. One or two 28 to 40px actions.

Logo alone at left, all links pushed right beside the action, which reads calm and confident. 64 to 88px tall, 13 to 16px muted links, 24 to 32px apart, a 1x14px divider before Log in, one 32 to 40px pill. Gutter equals the hero's left edge.

Compact global bar: 44px tall, 12px links at 80 percent ink spread evenly across a fixed 980px row with space-between, mark far left, search and bag far right, no CTA. Use saturate(1.8) blur(20px) on an 80 percent fill so colour tints it as content passes.

Wordmark dead centre on a 1fr auto 1fr grid, categories left, utilities right. 56 to 72px tall, 12 to 13px tracked caps or 16px text, 25px gaps, 10 to 24px side inset, no filled CTA or one 32px outlined pill. For retail, hospitality and food.

Three points: menu word with two-line icon at left, centred wordmark, one booking action at right. 56 to 73px tall, 14px labels, action a 42 to 50px near-square block or bold text. No link row. For hotels, restaurants and luxury, where the one decision is to book.

Logo left, then only the word Menu, a burger or one action at right, with no exposed links. No fill or border, 20 to 40px gutters, 14 to 17px labels. Use when the site has few pages or the work should fill the screen. Give the menu word a 44px target.

No bar: a line of small type floats on the page. 11 to 14px, caps tracked .08em or plain text, 35 to 56px gaps, no fill, border or button. Also works at display scale, 35 to 44px, as the header itself. Needs a quiet ground or a top scrim on images.

No bar: fixed items pinned to viewport corners at 16 to 32px insets, 11 to 16px type, content scrolling freely beneath. Logo in one corner, Contact in another, perhaps a clock or toggle. For portfolios and studios. Check every corner against every section for contrast.

Fixed transparent row set white with mix-blend-mode:difference, so each letter inverts over what passes beneath. 12 to 17px text, 15 to 32px margins, no fill. Keep grounds near white or near black, because mid greys and saturated colours turn muddy.

No fill or border: a 72px fixed bar over a 16 to 20px blur masked to fade out 30 to 130px below it. Links 14 to 15px. Nothing guarantees contrast, so flip ink and CTA per section by sampling what sits under the bar, with a 200ms transition.

One bar geometry, skin swapped per section: fill, links, CTA and rule change as sections pass, in 200ms. Either match the section colour so the bar melts into it, or invert on dark chapters. Mark sections with a data attribute and sample under the bar.

Starts clear over hero media with white links, becomes solid or blurred past 40px of scroll. 64 to 96px shrinking to 64 to 72px, 200 to 300ms on background and colour. Add a 1px rule or soft shadow only in the solid state. Logo and CTA swap colour with it.

Global bar plus a product row. Global 44 to 76px scrolls away, then a 44 to 66px row sticks: product name left at 15 to 21px, anchors right at 12 to 15px, current in ink, rest muted or accent, CTA at the end, blur or dashed rule between tiers.

Two stacked rows: a 24 to 64px utility or brand row over a 44 to 90px section row. Utility 10 to 13px, sections 14 to 18px, 1px rules between. For institutions, retail and magazines with many audiences. Keep both rows on the same page rails.

The bar changes job on scroll: full links at top, then only logo and CTA, or section anchors with an active state and a 2 to 3px progress line along the top edge. 56 to 72px, soft shadow, 200 to 300ms crossfade. For long pricing and product pages.

Search outranks links: a 36 to 48px field, 190 to 780px wide, filled or 1px outlined, with a keycap hint, sits centre or after the logo. 48 to 70px bar, 14px links, small icon tools. For docs, marketplaces and registries. Must be working search.

Shop bar: many plain categories, 11 to 16px, 20 to 40px apart, then an underlined search field or icon, account and bag with a count. 56 to 80px tall, no CTA because the categories are the action, one category in red or bold for sale. Dense but flat.

A developer's bar: 13 to 15px mono links, often caps, in a 56 to 64px bar on the page column, hairline below, radius 4. Actions show 16px keycaps beside search, sign up and download, or links take slash prefixes or bracket indices. Every control hints at a shortcut.

The nav is a table: cells split by 1px rules, logo in its own cell, links in equal cells of 100 to 240px, sometimes an inverted end cap for sign in. 44 to 112px tall, 12 to 16px mono or grotesk, radius 0 to 4. For archives, institutions and technical brands.

Links as objects: each a 28 to 40px chip or tag, radius 3 to 999, tinted or white with a 1px edge, 2 to 10px gaps, sometimes grouped in one capsule. Active chip one tone darker. Works over photographs with no bar behind, and can flank a centred logo.

The whole bar is the brand colour: 48 to 72px flat fill, no border, links in one ink at 14 to 16px, often lowercase or caps, one contrasting action. Makes the top edge the identity. Confirm 4.5:1 for links and repeat that colour lower on the page.

Always-open site map: 3 or 4 columns of two or three 13px links on 18px leading, no fill, aligned to the footer grid, or pictured items with a line glyph and sub-links. 80 to 100px tall, scrolls away. For small catalogues with few destinations.

Nav on the viewport's bottom edge: 42 to 54px strip, 11 to 15px links, name at one end, the key action at the other. For single-screen sites and local services, where call or book stays under the thumb. Add safe-area padding on phones.

The bar's main control is a switch of audience, product, category or filter: a 44px tinted track with an active pill, three to five icon tabs with an underline, or five evenly spaced 12px filters beside search. Use when the first decision is who you are or what you want.

The bar imitates an operating system or live instrument: 36 to 44px, inset 8px at radius 6 like a menu bar, or icon cells split by rules, or a live clock and online count in mono. Only when the whole site commits to that metaphor.

Something hangs off the top edge: links in a dark tab about 640x46 with concave corners cut into the page, a round seal overhanging the row, a half-disc crest, or a tiled frieze. One shaped object gives identity without adding chrome.

Fixed bar inset 8 to 24px from the top and 8 to 60px at the sides, 60 to 76px tall, radius 12 to 20, fill at 72 to 85 percent with 12 to 20px blur, 1px ring at 8 percent. 14 to 15px links, 36px CTA inset 8 to 14px from the end.

At top a transparent full-width row. Past 40px of scroll it draws in to a 980 to 1380px capsule, 16 to 25px from the top, 54 to 64px tall, radius 27 to 100, 70 to 80 percent fill, 20px blur, soft shadow. Animate max-width 450ms, fill 250ms.

Small pill at top centre, 40 to 58px tall, 420 to 680px wide, full radius, 12 to 24px from the top: logo, 12 to 15px links, inset 32 to 36px CTA. White with soft shadow, or translucent with blur. Four links at most. The logo can stay outside it.

Precise rather than cute: a tray 450 to 1100px wide, 56 to 76px tall, radius 3 to 8, 1px hairline, flat or 50 to 60 percent fill with blur, no shadow. The logo can sit centre between two words. Reads as a label on a technical drawing.

Nav as a segmented control: fixed 480x40 near-ink bar, radius 8, 2px padding, five 94px segments with 1px gaps, active segment a paper tile at radius 6. The thumb slides on scroll-spy. Legible over any section. For one-page sites with five sections or fewer.

No bar: logo and action become separate floating objects in opposite corners, 12 to 40px from the edges. A 48 to 52px white circle mark collapses from the wordmark, a 40 to 48px action pill opposite, soft shadow. Nothing between them, so sections keep full width.

Two separate bars side by side: a long nav bar and a short actions bar, 60px tall, inset 16px, radius 8, 6px gap, sometimes joined by a short coloured dash. The gap is the identity. Use with a strong grid and one small accent.

A floating element for sections: centred row of 36px pills, 14px text, 18px gaps, solid current pill, in a frosted band; or a white 64px card 8px from the top holding anchors and a CTA after the global bar leaves. Sticks under the page's own chrome.

Fixed pill at bottom centre, 480x52, 18px above the edge: name, 14px links, toggle, translucent so each panel tints it. Reserve a safe zone so it never covers CTAs or copy. For portfolios. On phones it competes with browser chrome.

One action follows the reader: a bottom-centre 480 to 510px prompt field, 48 to 56px tall, with a 32px accent button, or a 224x60 pill with a founder's photo, or a small chip 20 to 24px from a corner. Only when the action is the product.

Compact lozenge: 240 to 380px wide, 40 to 52px tall, radius 6 to 12, fixed at top centre, holding mark, wordmark and a two-line menu icon, perhaps a clock. No links exposed, so sections keep full width. The menu opens from it.

Expressive capsule with visible construction: black 82px bar, radius 40, dashed vertical seams dividing logo, links and CTAs like a ticket stub, or a 2px outlined capsule with a ringed burger overlapping its end. Only on expressive consumer pages.

One line on near-black above the nav: 38 to 48px, 14px/500 white, centred, an arrow that moves 3px on hover or an underlined link, optional close 24px from the right. Ties to dark CTAs. Truncate with an ellipsis on phones rather than wrapping.

Strip sits behind the page: a fixed 44 to 76px band with the page sheet above it at 24 to 40px rounded top corners, so the site looks lifted. 14 to 16px text, one 32px white pill. Keep sheet and nav the same colour.

A deep tone of the brand rather than its full colour: 36 to 65px, oxblood from a red CTA or teal-black from a cyan one, 14 to 16px cream or tinted text, small coloured arrow. Reads as brand, not warning. One step off a dark page is enough.

Saturated brand colour, 32 to 60px, ink or white 14 to 16px text, one arrow or pill. Works when it is the only bright colour on the first screen. Keep it above 30px with 12px minimum text, because 9px caps on an 18px strip looks like a template.

Quiet tint with ink text: 34 to 48px, 3 to 8 percent of a hue, 14px centred, underlined link, close at right, optional 1px rule. News without urgency. Use when the page already has strong colour below.

A small tag starts the line: an 18 to 28px pill or outlined label at 11 to 12px saying what kind of news this is, then a 14px sentence and underlined link. The tag can be the only accent. Aligns left to the logo or centres in a 34 to 60px strip.

Texture at the ends, text in the middle: a 36 to 52px strip with halftone dots shrinking inward over 230 to 300px, brand grain, or a 2px gradient hairline at the base. A real material, not a flat fill. Dots must shrink, because a uniform grid looks like a bug.

Not full-bleed: a 32 to 62px notice inset to the page container, radius 4 to 12, tinted, or white on a tinted page, 14px centred line, close at right. Reads as a card above the hero. Keep its edges on the page rail.

News under the nav rather than above it: 38 to 52px, page tint or hairlines only, 14px centred, bold underlined link. Scrolls away while the nav stays. Keeps the top edge clean. Mono caps reads as machine output.

Not a bar: a 24 to 36px pill 24px above the H1, full radius, tinted or 1px edge, 13px text, small dot or arrow. Stays on the hero's axis. Common to the point of cliche, so use it only for real news with a date or a name.

Continuous loop of offers: 16 to 56px strip, 12 to 14px mono or caps, 24 to 48px gaps, separators, faded right edge, pause button at right. Reads as ticker tape. Must pause on hover and stop under reduced motion.

Two to four offers in one slot: 28 to 46px, 11 to 14px centred, thin chevrons at both ends, or a vertical crossfade every 5 to 7 seconds. Keep the paging controls, because auto-rotation alone hides offers.

A strip that also carries utilities: loyalty or store links left, centred offer, region right, 32 to 52px, 11 to 14px. Folds chrome into one line so the main nav holds only products. Region switchers add a flag select and a round arrow.

Pinned to the viewport base: 42 to 60px, one offer or question left, action and close right, 1px top rule or solid fill, appearing after first scroll. Move it to the top on phones to avoid the browser bar.

A statement, not a promo: availability or a notice in the site's own voice, 44 to 52px, left aligned, closed by a 1px rule; or a filled alert with icon and close when it is truly urgent. No arrow and no offer.

Page-wide band flush under the bar, same colour as the bar, hairline base, no shadow or radius. Three to five text columns from the logo's left edge at 266px steps: 14px grey label over 20px links on 32px pitch, or 14 to 16px on 28px. Page veiled 60 percent.

Full-width sheet growing from a 44px bar, 480 to 530px tall: one large list at 24/600 on 38px pitch, then two small columns at 12/600 on 24px, 12px grey labels, all on the 980px rail. Page behind takes a 20px blur plus a dark veil.

Floating 530 to 900px panel, radius 4 to 12, 1px edge: three or four plain link columns split by vertical hairlines, 12px grey or mono labels, 15px links on 32 to 39px pitch, no icons. Optional 53px tinted footer strip with small 30px pill buttons.

Titles with grey lines and no icons: 800 to 1200px panel, radius 12, 14 to 15px title over a 12 to 14px grey description, three to six columns under small labels, 50 to 60px pitch. Use when names alone do not explain the product.

The common product menu: 560 to 900px panel, radius 8 to 12, rows of a 28 to 32px icon tile, 14px title and 12 to 13px grey one-liner, two or three columns, 50 to 60px pitch, mono or caps labels. Every icon different, all one stroke weight.

Panel 700 to 1000px wide: about six rows of icon, title and one-liner on 60px pitch, then one or two feature tiles 300 to 400px wide, radius 8, showing real product, a graphic or a release. The tile is the only loud thing. Rotate it with news.

Entries are pictures: 830 to 1160px panel, radius 12 to 20, three to five equal cards, 200x133 photos at radius 8 or 254px tinted illustration tiles, 32px gaps, 15px title, 13px line, 49px footer strip. Needs real imagery, because gradients read as placeholders.

Store drawer: full width, 400 to 520px tall, four or five link columns, 12px mono or caps headers, 16px links on 33px pitch, two or three portrait photos 210x263 with captions at right, page blurred and dimmed. First column holds edits and new arrivals.

Left rail of 5 to 8 categories, 36px rows, 200px wide, active pill. Hovering swaps the middle list of title and line on 62px pitch, plus a 240x434 portrait at right. Panel keeps one width across triggers, so nothing jumps. For broad catalogues and industries.

Full-width panel of bordered tiles: one dark lead tile 280px wide holding an overview and two rows, then a 2x3 grid of 480x76 cells, 8px gaps, square corners, 1px line, title and grey line left, small glyph right. Reads as a control panel.

Zones by tone, not lines: 860 to 1000px panel, radius 14 to 20, 8px padding, inner well one tone step off at radius 8 to 16, or a tinted right rail, with a footer strip beneath. Three columns of about 280px with hairlines between; rail holds secondary links.

Small honest menu: 120 to 300px wide, radius 4 to 12, 6 to 10px under the trigger and left-aligned to it, soft shadow, 14px rows on 30 to 34px pitch, plain links or 16px icons. Right for four to eight items. Never stretch it to fill.

Bar and menu are one object: the bar sits inside a panel that opens to about 1262x780, radius 6, big soft shadow, page blurred. Five columns, hairline-ruled 14px headings, accent link over grey line, tinted right rail, footer row. Or the whole bar floods into a sheet.

The menu shows a live thing: an upcoming event card with avatar, date and join button, a changelog feed with thumbnails, blog titles with excerpts, or a product with price and shop button. Use when fresh content beats a list of pages.

No panel: a plain list appears on the hero under the trigger, or a stack of 44px black chips with 4px gaps, or the page swaps to a field of names. Fades and rises 8px. Only over calm images and with few items.

Full-height sheet: 4 to 6 rows at 16 to 18px on 48 to 76px pitch, hairlines between, plus or chevron at right on groups, plain rows below, two CTAs pinned at the base. Rows stagger 45ms and settle by 320 to 900ms. The default for products.

Full screen, 4 to 8 rows at 16 to 20px on 44 to 57px pitch, hairlines, no CTA inside because one stays in the bar, chevrons only on groups. Fast and honest, appears in one step. Put something at the base so it does not look empty.

No accordions, everything visible at once under small grey labels: 14px labels, 24/500 links on 44px pitch, group gaps 28 to 40px, sheet scrolls past the fold. Near instant, under 120ms. Best for dark tools and sites with 10 to 15 links.

Actions sit above the links: two 48px pills or one 44px button directly under the header, then 16 to 20px rows on 57 to 77px pitch with arrows or chevrons. Use when most phone visitors came to sign up.

Links as headline: 40 to 64px display type, tracking -.03 to -.045em, 44 to 66px pitch, no rows or icons, left aligned, filling the screen from the top. Base: a hairline, then small account links. Reveal with a fast clip or fade. Six short words at most.

The menu is a room of brand colour: full-screen flat fill, 28 to 44px links, small secondary links below, close mark in place of the burger. Entered by a wash or stacked bands, 120 to 900ms. Spend it once on a page.

Numbered rows: 01 to 06 in 10 to 12px beside 32 to 56px heavy or serif links, 60 to 97px pitch, hairlines, an optional one-line subtitle, language or clock pinned at the base. Reads like a contents page. For agencies and hotels.

A curved mask sweeps down, then 38 to 44px serif links fade in from the top on 57 to 80px pitch, with hairlines, circled arrows and one full-width CTA. 320ms sweep, stagger to 900ms. Uses clip-path, so drop it under reduced motion.

The menu is a card under the bar: 8 to 16px side inset, radius 12 to 16, rows at 16/600 on 48 to 60px pitch, CTAs inside, page blurred 8px behind. Lighter than a takeover. Floating bars expand into it. Cap its height and let it scroll.

Menu opens in the flow: rows drop under the header and push the hero down, 40 to 57px pitch, hairlines, no scrim, complete by 120ms. Simple and robust, with no scroll lock. Best for short lists of four to six.

A sheet from the right at 80 to 100 percent width over a scrim, 200 to 320ms ease-out: 16 to 17px rows on 48 to 53px pitch, chevrons, hairlines, empty middle, CTAs pinned at the base. Keep a 30 to 60px peek of the page so it reads as a layer.

Left drawer or inline panel holding the same tree as desktop docs: 14 to 15px rows on 32 to 36px pitch, caps group labels, active row tinted, scrolled to the current page. Keeps the reader's place rather than offering a marketing list.

Rows carry more than a name: 106px tinted cards with title, line and illustration, or 44px icon tiles with descriptions on 80px pitch, or chip grids by section. Then plain links, then CTAs at the base. For products whose names alone do not sell.

No panel: full-width pills pop in one at a time over the live page, 60 to 80px tall, 8 to 16px gaps, centred labels. Playful and easy on the thumb. Four items only. Stagger 60 to 100ms with a slight scale.

Search leads: a 44 to 56px field at the top of the sheet, focused, then quick links with arrows, or tabs for docs, guides and reference. For stores and docs where visitors know what they want. Keep results in the same sheet.

Menu anchored low: 30px links on 40px pitch in the lower half with chevrons far right, or a rounded-top sheet with close controls at its base. Everything sits in thumb reach, and the empty space above is fine.

Sticky 222 to 300px left column on long pages: 15px links on 27 to 28px pitch, 15/600 group heads, active in accent or with a 2px tick hung outside. List masks out over 64px at the base above a hairline and one pinned link.

Fixed 80 to 92px left rail bounded by a full-height 1px line: a tall monogram at top, Menu at the base, nothing between. Content scrolls right of the line. Reads as a printed margin. App version: 88px rail, 24px icons on 72px steps, active pill.

A fixed 200 to 300px column replaces the top bar: logo, 6 to 20 plain links at 15 to 20px, no active chrome, actions pinned to the base, 1px rule or none. Content scrolls beside it. For tools, libraries and indexes.
Site sections as desktop files: 56px illustrated icons with 13 to 14px shadowed labels in columns at both edges on an 84px pitch, over a wallpaper. A whole-site metaphor, never a garnish.

Navigation held on the frame: rotated 14px labels at mid height 57px from each edge, fixed monogram letters at 50px insets, or small margin notes. Ink recolours per section. For architecture and portfolios with few pages.

A small index on the side: 12 to 16px numbers or ticks on 14 to 39px pitch, active one ringed, bracketed or longer, neighbours fading by distance, keyboard hints optional. Reads as a contact sheet or picker wheel. For decks and scroll stories.

A band of tabs under the main nav for parts of one thing: 40 to 58px, 11 to 14px tracked caps or text, active underline, sticky. Brand fill for restaurant menus, hairline for museums, 40px product thumbnails for ranges.

A tab fixed to the viewport edge: 40 to 52px wide, 198 to 270px tall, 12 to 18px rotated or stacked label, inner corners radius 8. One persistent job such as hours or shop. Vertical scripts make it natural.

Navigation placed in the page as a list: 36/40 links in a 700px column on 101px pitch, 1px rules, no icons, an Index label at left. Or a chapter list at 17/25 on each opener. For sites that read like a book.
App or docs tree: 13 to 14px rows on 29 to 32px pitch, 12px caps labels, active row a flat tint at radius 2 to 8 with a 2 to 3px accent bar, children indented 22px on a guide line.

Fixed 288px rail: 12px mono caps group labels tracked .1em, 14px links on 32px pitch indented 16px behind a 1px line, active link 500 with an ink segment on the line, 32px between groups. No icons, no chevrons, every page visible.

300px rail, 1px rule: 36px filter field with a slash keycap, 12px caps labels, 14px rows on 34px pitch, line icons, right chevrons, active row tinted at radius 8. Filtering narrows the tree. For docs with hundreds of pages. Can float as a panel inset 8px.

Wide 300 to 348px column: 15px section heads with 18px outline icons, children 14px muted on 33px pitch flush with the icon, not indented, chevrons far right, active in accent with no fill. Or nine flat top links, a divider, then collapsible groups.

240 to 260px rail, 14px rows on 32 to 37px pitch, active row a soft filled pill at radius 8 to 999 with darker text, 13 to 14px group labels, no guide lines. Soft and product-like. Fade the rail at top and bottom.

Docs layout: 48 to 56px top bar, 260 to 304px left rail, 576 to 730px reading column, 200 to 240px right outline. Rails fixed, only content scrolls. Content sits off-centre to keep a 65 character measure.

Right outline: 13 to 14px grey links on 28 to 32px pitch beside a 1px line, nested items indented 12px, current heading turns ink with a dark segment on the line. Starts level with the page title. Hidden on narrow screens.
Three-level docs: top bar, a 44 to 48px row of product tabs at 13 to 14px with a 1px accent underline on a hairline, then left rail and right outline. For docs that span several products.
Docs home as an index, not a tree: grouped cards or a plain grid, each entry an 8px colour square, 16/600 name and 12 to 13px grey line. Everything visible at a glance. Empty cells stay empty.
Contents page of a book: 18/500 chapter titles, 3px dotted leader to a right-aligned 14px page number, 50px pitch. Use once, for handbooks and long reads.
Header built for reading: 44 to 65px, 13px breadcrumb, copy-page button, search with slash key, plan or version switch, split into cells by 1px rules or quiet spacing. Utilities only, no marketing.
Horizontal filter for lists such as changelogs: 15px text filters in muted ink, 16px gaps, active just brightens with no pill, 280x40 pill search at right with a bare subscribe bell.

Rebuild the app in DOM at true scale, 1200-1320px wide, with its top edge at 58% of the viewport and its base cut by the fold. 1px ink-8% border, radius 12-14, no shadow. 240px sidebar with 13/28 rows; main pane a raised sheet inset 8px. One live state.

Outer shell 1080-1248px, tinted ink-5%, radius 16, 1px line. 32-34px title bar with dots or a breadcrumb. App sheet inset 8px on three sides, radius 8-10, its own 1px line. 250px sidebar on a half-step tint, 14/28 rows. Never show the bottom edge.

Window or shell with 1px line and radius 16-24 dissolves into the page: mask the lower third, or the right and bottom edges, to page colour. Text stays real and dims with distance. No hard base, no shadow halo, no fake window edge.

Column-wide plate 480-640px tall, painted image or tinted panel, radius 0 or 48. Window inset 24-35px at the sides and 50px at the top, cropped by the plate base. Radius 12, 1px edge, soft 18/50 shadow. All colour lives on the plate; the UI stays neutral.

Panel 660-1390px, radius 8-12, real texture or interior photograph with fine grain. App window centred or inset 48-90px, soft shadow, radius 8-12. Optional faux 11px menu bar across the top. Texture stays low contrast, so the window keeps the eye.

Dashboard 1080-1200px with no chrome, radius 8-12, layered shadow, real nav, chart and table. It straddles a section change: the next section's angled edge or colour break hides its base. It must never simply end inside one section.

Main window 800-1100px wide plus one smaller panel 296-436px overlapping an edge by 40-120px. Panel has its own fill, radius 12-16 and a soft shadow, or on dark a lighter fill and no shadow. Window shows context, panel shows the feature.

No window. A tinted panel about 845px wide is the app: oversized search line in display type, a hairline, then 4 masonry columns of 170px with a 16px gap mixing photos, quotes, highlighted notes and price tags.

1080px browser frame, app dimmed by a dark gradient that fades to page colour at the base. Centred 500px white modal, 1px accent border, soft matching glow, 56px rows split by hairlines. Supporting logos overlap its lower edge.

Window about 1230px, radius 24, 1px ink-14% border, dots left, view toggles right. Three panes: 200px file list, mono code centre, rendered output right on a soft radial glow. Selecting a file tints it and changes code and output together.

Black stage about 1190x550, radius 20, one dim colour glow in a corner. Real editor window offset right and down, clipped by the right and bottom edges, 1px light border, radius 20. Sliders and toggles stay legible at true scale.

Row of 3-4 equal tabs, 48px tall with 1px dividers, docked to the frame top and sharing its border. Active tab tinted with a 2px accent top line, label 16/600. Screenshot inset 40px inside the frame with its own 1px border. Tabs swap the whole view.

Product 750-900px wide, flush to the right gutter or bleeding off the viewport. Small 11-13px UI left unretouched, 1px border, radius 10. Copy large on the left. No shadow on dark pages; light chrome bar optional on light ones.
Dark screen 800-880px wide, 3-4px bezel in a pale accent, soft outer glow, radius 20, no window chrome. One small notch or hardware hint at most. It reads as a device without drawing one.

Recorded product video 1000-1200px wide with UI text readable at 11-12px, radius 12-24, cropped or fully framed. A 36-40px circular pause button sits in a corner. Use a different recording per section; never one clip reused.

Screenshot about 400x300, radius 12, soft shadow. Behind it two flat plates rotated -3 and +3 degrees, one dark and one accent, each showing a single corner. Repeat the identical stack on every feature row.

Two-up small windows 8-12 radius, 1px border, true chrome colours per channel, around 11px type. Use skeleton bars only when the point is the channel rather than the content. Prefer one real window over this.

Grey well or hairline tile, radius 14-20. One real component centred at true 13-15px: white card, 1px border, radius 12-14. No scale, tilt or window chrome. Give each well one state, such as a tooltip or a checked row.

Redraw product UI in brand geometry: deep brand fill, 2px white outline and one accent chip; or a notched card with an inverted corner; or 1.5px ink-stroked widgets. Shape and colour come from the brand, the data stays real.

Portrait or textured photo, radius 6-20. One sharp card pinned low, inset 20px, radius 16, 60px rows of 14px type. Or 270px frosted cards at 85% white. Photo stays at real scale, card carries all the detail, and one row fades to imply life.

One menu or dialog at 1-2x over its app faded to 30%: 392px white menu, radius 12, soft shadow, selected row filled with a 2px accent bar, shortcut chips. A large cursor rests on the row. Keycaps may overlap the edge.

White nodes 160-216 by 52-74px, radius 6-12, 1px line, active 1px accent. Rounded elbow connectors, 7px ports. Status chips above nodes: green completed, accent running. Unfired paths grey. 16-28px dot grid on a tint. Bleed off one edge.

Panel 292-538px, radius 12-16, 1px line. Dark or tinted user bubble, plain 13-14/18-20 reply with bold findings, a Thinking line, a Changes box with Undo, composer with model picker and 24px icons. No avatars on messages.

Table bleeding off a tinted cell's right and bottom edges. 13-14px, rows 36-38px or 60 relaxed, hairlines, tabular right-aligned numbers, 12px grey headers, 16px logos, tinted score chips. Invent specific entities. One row selected. Crop it; do not fade early.

Real working UI inline with no frame: a 1136px search with four selects, a count and a pager; or 52x76 date chips with masked ends; or a typed block with a caret. Full size, keyboard reachable, and it must work on a phone.

Stack of 51-60px rows or sentence-rows with status chips, each row dimmer than the last: 100, 70, 40, 15%. 12px mono names, 9-12px status chips, timestamps. Mask or blur the base. A new row can arrive at the top.
