spec: Two or three white panels with 10-13px type, radius 6-14, overlapping at two depths on a rich gradient that leaks around them, soft tinted shadow, cropped by the card edge. Real labels, segmented controls, plans and prices.

Panel 540-1080px, radius 8, 1px dividers, real settings: sliders, count pills, ticks or ring progress, accordion rows. True 13-15px text. Right half may tint one step. Around 60px soft shadow. Ghost the chrome to 10% contrast, if used.

UI drawn as a physical thing: a 384px note with a perforated edge, cards rotated 5 degrees, tags rotated 10 hanging off a sheet, soft 20/40 shadow. Specific human content. A slight break of the grid gives flat UI a handled quality.

Product panel 400-480px wide with no frame on page colour. Mask right and bottom into the page. Text 11-13px, dim except one focal row at full ink. Optional raised card in front with a lighter fill, no glow. 60px air above and below.

One real control scaled 1.5-2x inside a tile and cropped by its edge: a pill, keycap or field with a click ring and cursor. Frosted white fields, radius 14, or about 100px of air each side if uncropped. No window.

Real UI cards joined by 1px dashed or thin accent connectors. Greyed source pills feed a 240px status card with a 44px icon tile and four 11px mono states on a dot-line. White cards, soft shadow, pale panel, radius 4-16.

Vertical list on a 1px connector with 32px icon tiles, then either token chips forming a sentence at 16-18px, or Failed, Retry and Paid steps with dates at the right. One step boxed in 1px accent, radius 8.

Tray 692x406, radius 16, 1px border, holding two equal 322px white windows with one prompt and two outcomes. Or a 1078px container split 50/50, pale column and dark column. A single accent marks the better result.

Single white card 340-440px, radius 24-32, hue-tinted 24px shadow, on a pale wash. 40px drawn icon tile, 16px name, 14px muted detail, right-aligned amount. One object, no frame. Add a faded card behind for depth.

The product's own overlay as a page constant: about 110px round camera over a shot with a control pill, or a 366x60 dock of 40px icons, idle at 40% with an active dot, or a 296px widget 24px from the corner.

Two or three cards, radius 20-24, the middle one wider and overlapping: status chips, 40px metric in accent, bar spark with 1hr, 30m, Now labels, shadow 0 8 24. Or dark tiles that overlap and bleed off every edge.

400px tinted card, radius 16. Three 52px chips, radius 12, active one solid. A white result bubble below at 16/600 changes per chip. Or a prompt box with template chips and theme swatches. One control, one visible change.

Code beside its live output, split 50/50 or 40/60. Window about 1150px, radius 18, 1px line, filename bar, mono 13-14/20-24. Output is real: rendered email, running visualiser, flow diagram on a dotted pane. Change one and the other responds.

Code pane about 555x340 beside a 225-258px rail of topics or files: 11-12px mono caps rows with hairlines, or 16px items, active row tinted with a 2px bar. A note pinned to the rail base. Fade the code at the bottom.

White card, 1px hairline, radius 8-12, 48px header with dots, 13px mono filename and a real control at right, such as a run-target select. Mono 13/20 with three token colours. Clip mid-line at the cell bottom, or pair with a chat column.

Panel 544-1024px, radius 12-24, 1px line. Language or framework tabs: 60x56 icon tiles or 90px tabs split by hairlines, active brightened, copy icon right. Mono 13-14/20-22, line numbers at 30% ink, one accent for strings.

Full-bleed saturated band. Copy left, H2 at 32px. Right, a near-black card about 600x326, radius 8, language header over hairline, mono 12, soft shadow. The endpoint string changes over time. Or pair two unequal windows, top-aligned at different heights.

POST pill, mono URL, hairline, 14-16px mono JSON with a single warm string colour, hairline, footer with install command, tiny sparkline and language circles. Or a deep tinted pane with one call, dim line numbers 1-10 and a block caret.

Dark code panel about 500px, radius 4-12, with run and copy icons, laid over a light dashboard or brand card. Three depths: terminal, object, dashboard bleeding off the right. One tinted panel behind holds them together.

Panel about 880px, radius 12, mono 14/24, line numbers at 30% ink. Changed rows get a tinted band plus a coloured gutter number, and the exact token a 30% tint. Keep syntax colour on. Right column fades out, overlapping a real list at 85%.

Near-black outer radius 12 with 30px header of filename and copy icon. Inner lighter panel inset 4px, radius 8, mono 14/20. Highlighted lines get a 2px accent bar and tinted row. Works repeated, as every block in a doc.

Frameless grey mono 14/20 on page grain, or a black pane at 16/24. Each step gets a 2px rounded left bracket: green done, red with 10% tint running. Status pills such as COMPLETED | 1.2S hang in the left margin. State is the only colour.

Code panel cropped by the card edge on the left 43%, top-right radius 20, 1px top highlight. 11px language tabs. Every line at 25% ink except the single method line at full ink. Serves as texture with one readable point.

Panel about 1200px, 1px line, radius 4. 44px tinted header: mono POST, path, two payload toggles. Request on white, 201 response on a pale success tint, 13/22 mono, one live value highlighted. Toggles swap the payload.

Box 680x48-60, 1px line, radius 0-4, mono 14, copy icon in its own divided cell at right. No window dots, prompt symbol or syntax colour. Paper-like sites can add a hard 3px offset shadow with no blur.
Inside body copy: mono 13-16px in a 26px chip, radius 4-6, 1px line, faint fill, optional copy icon at right. It sits within the line height, so the paragraph keeps its rhythm.

Warm-black panel, radius 12, mono 12/19. Header: host, region, outlined status pill with dot. Subheader: cron plus cpu and mem bars. Log: grey comments, accent prompt, green bullets, tree connectors, block cursor. The last step is in progress.

The command is the hero action. 52px pill, hairline plus soft shadow, muted $, mono 14, 16px copy icon. Or 60px ink block, mono 16, accent $, copy in a separate clipped-corner cell, OS toggle below. Or a quiet 35px bar under the CTAs.

Box about 720px with 13px mono tabs for npm, pnpm and friends, active one boxed or underlined, hairline, one coloured command line, copy tile bottom right. Optional dashed frame offset 5px outside a solid one.

Module about 745px, radius 14, 2px near-black frame. Mono caps labels, a grey prompt pill with three agent icons and copy button, then two 1px command boxes with one syntax colour. Repeat it verbatim at the closing CTA.
Framework dropdown, a one-line 16px sentence, then a dark code block about 950x120 with copy icon. Two brand characters lean in from both sides. The joke is on the block, not beside it.

Dark terminal, radius 6, three dots, mono 12, green diamonds on steps, later lines fading out. Overlapped by the resulting UI, as a skeleton card in a tray. Spinner and a short caption below. Depth comes from overlap.

Window about 410px, radius 8-12, dots, mono 13/23, credible output, rising from the card base on a pale fade or grain panel and cropped by the edge. A separate chip such as a ready line can float above.
Panel 720-1120px, radius 4, mono 14-16 typing one command with a caret, then output. Prompt chips with line number, truncated text and Copy sit below. Start half-typed so the panel is never blank.

Phone drawn as a thin steel rim on black, about 440px wide, cropped by the section base. Black screen, one 48px number with small decimals, grey round actions. Or a 1px white-40% outline with no bezel over a shader.

Window at the fold, phone 200-220px wide overlapping its lower right by 60px, 2px rim, radius 40, real content at about 14px. Depth comes from overlap alone. On light pages add a soft shadow and floating action pills between them.
Real hands hold a tablet or phone tilted about 8 degrees, rising from the section bottom, cropped. Legible UI on screen, cool rim light. Centred two-tone 40px heading above: white, then 50% white.

Phone frame on a pale ground, screen faded to 30%. White cards 120x168, radius 24, overlap both phone edges with 76px progress rings and short labels. Or chips 196x66, radius 8, soft shadow, at staggered heights over a bezel.

Video phone about 270x555, radius 32, white bezel, 3px gradient stroke drawn along only part of the edge. Landscape tablet tucked behind, joined by a thin line. Overlays such as a pose skeleton and 9/10 score sit on the video.

Phone with no hardware detail, about 300x590, radius 44, 4px pale rim, wide soft shadow. Real checkout at 12-14px: wallet button, stacked 1px inputs, Pay button. A receipt card behind and a toast crossing both. Right edge sits on the page guide.

Three phones. Either fanned, centre forward at 400px, side phones 120-200px lower, clipped, bottoms fading to the ground; or stacked three-quarter renders on the centre axis with elliptical floor shadows. UI redrawn in brand style.

Skew or rotate 8 degrees, black face, 1px bright rim highlight on one corner, a second offset outline behind, cropped by the card base. Or a macro 3D render at a steep angle filling the frame. Never a gentle floating tilt.

Phone centred under the heading, cropped by scroll or by a 466px tile, radius 20. Feature notes flank left and right in staggered rows, active note on a pale card, each with a 56px icon square. Offset the tops.
Horizontal rail of editor window, phone and CLI, all dark, top aligned, 240-520px wide, 14px captions beneath, clipped at the right to hint at more. The same session content appears on each surface.

The same phone, about 245px, holds its position across chapters while the screen swaps: product, payment sheet, coupon, dashboard. Oversized props tied to each message sit around it. Copy scrolls past.
Black-bezel tablets, radius 32, cropped by section edges across a two-colour split, holding real charts and order lists. Devices run off screen and are never shown whole.

Square photo about 615px with white pills floating over and past its edges, soft shadow: words, swatch plus word. Height varies 22-50px to imply depth, and grows on scroll. Annotation without leader lines.

Exploded render about 560px centred, with six callouts outside it: 12px mono caps, grey [+] prefix, on a 1px rule about 300px long ending in a 3px dot on the part. Uneven heights, both sides. Or run dotted lines up to outlined SKU pills.

Key UI rows lift out as wider white bands, bracketed by 1px frames with 6px corner handles. Or corner reticles with a centred cross and 10px labels. Or layer a tinted redline box labelled with a mono width.

Isometric slabs stacked, with 16px labels and short dash leaders at left. Fill steps through one hue from white to full accent, so the diagram is the explanation. One slab in the accent marks the new layer. Works at 390px.

Native diagram: mono boxes radius 4-6, 1px lines with small nodes, pale numbered discs 01-03 along the path, dashed trust boundary, one accent VERIFIED tag, tracked 11px mono captions. Pin beside scrolling copy.
Dim dark UI shot with a circular lens about 300px, 4px gradient ring, showing the key lines enlarged at full brightness. The lens says which detail matters without a caption.
Snippet about 480px with only a 1px left and bottom rule, a pale red error row with a red bar. Accent mono notes at 14-16px rotated 3-4 degrees sit in the margins, linked by hand-drawn black arrows.

Rebuilt IDE about 975px. Inactive panes under a tinted wash, active pane pure. White 390px callout, radius 4, glowing accent edge, 26px mono title, 16px copy. A cursor arrow travels between stops as scroll advances.
Three columns: 20px paragraph, three verbs stacked at 56px with the active word white and others 25%, then a 280px dark device showing the matching controls. Scroll advances the verb.

spec: Room render or photo about 800px, radius 14-20. Rings 30px translucent with 14px white centres on each part, matched by a card alongside. Or green skeleton dots with a counter overlaid on a person.

Frame about 576x464 with deep fill, 2px rim, radius 24, hairline spectrum top and bottom. Two overlapping screens inside, light over dark, real data. A simple variant sets a small grey label left and a large photo right, alternating.

Dot field 16px pitch. Nodes radius 12, 1px border, mono 15px real identifiers, 8px square status dots. 1px grey arrows with tiny heads. Use actual state names. Ghost unused nodes as outlines fading into the grid.

Sphere of 2-4px dots with continents in a dot matrix. Small chips with mono 10px city, department and local-currency amount pin to dots, or 10px accent squares mark regions with a scrolling mono country list beside it.

1px ink box, 46px tab row with active tab solid. Rows 44px: name plus mono version, 28px tinted track, solid bar on one shared scale, right-aligned mono time. Winner in accent. Axis below, then one line of test conditions and a reproduce link.

Dark panel, radius 8-12, a real chart type: beeswarm of 5px dots with dim stepped percentiles, box-and-whisker with mono medians, heatmap of square cells. Footer legend explains it. Another panel fades behind at 50%.

One line 1.5-2px, optional fill fading to near-white, four ring markers or a live end dot, hairline grid, 12px axis labels, caption half accent, half ink. Width up to 1130px. Or a word set large over the line.
Box about 700px, 1px border at ink-6%, no radius. 37px rows: grey rank, 9px hue square, 13px name, 11px grey qualifier, right-aligned 110px bar in the same hue, 13px percent. 1px row rules.

Logo at centre with 1px spokes to 22px branches, each spraying finer spokes to 14px leaves. Labels fade from ink to 30% with depth and drift in on scroll. Or three concentric arcs, solid, dashed and dotted, carrying 24px logo chips.

Six equal cells split by 1px rules: 11-12px uppercase label, 18-20/700 value, 12px delta with coloured arrow. Selected cell tinted, radius 6-8, drives the chart below: 1.5px line, 10% fill, faint grid. Data has weekly rhythm.
A tiny widget with real data: 46px dial with one needle under 14px mono readout, or 197x35 sparkline with a 2.5px line and tinted fill and no axes, or four mono label-value rows at 21px pitch.

Descending isometric bars in 1px dotted outline on black, no axes, with only the winner solid and labelled in accent. Or a greyscale diagram with one dark outline, or a 230px outline pie with one accent slice.

Two 544px outlined panels of small rounded cells. One lights scattered rows, the other whole columns. Or dashed tiles with accent-tint fills and accent mono captions. No numbers: the arrangement argues.

Card up to 1080px, radius 8. Pill toggle switches scenarios. Solid history, dashed path, pale projection, soft filled areas. One 1px accent callout box with a vertical leader to a dot explains the key region.
2px line with end dot over a dotted 1px line, fine vertical hatching filling only the gap between them. 12px legend at the base, one baseline rule, no axes or gridlines. No colour needed.
Strip about 890x80 of 100 thin vertical bars, white with a soft tint midway. 54px/400 figure to its right with a 14px grey caption. Three 14px links with external icons below.
Grouped bars 44px wide with 4px gaps: yours in the accent, rivals in a warm grey. Rival logos sit inside bar tops. 12px bold mono values above, hairline gridlines, underlined group labels below.

Pale surface card 328x248, radius 16, 1.5px border. Range capsules at left, 9px mono labels, pale in-range zone, one dot joined by a 1px line to a later dot, date ticks below. Add a pause control if it animates.
Regions in 2px ink outline on a pale blob, one highlighted with 8% fill, white card with region name and price. Or a dark map with numbered clusters and a search overlay, radius 12.

CSS phone or nodes with concentric 1px rings, labelled pills attached by 1px lines with end dots. A small amount chip travels along the line, then rows update in sequence. Dashed variants work on saturated plates, in page type.

Composer types real prompts at 24-58ms a character with a slower pause on spaces, then send arrow fills, a shimmering Thinking line, then the answer. Panel tint changes per task. Modify and Replay buttons below. Start from a partial line.

Real DOM app window plays itself: a cursor moves on a 0.9s eased path, clicks, selection moves, inspector swaps with a 220ms crossfade, breadcrumb updates. Loop every 3-4s per step. 36-44px circular pause control. Rest on a designed frame.

Shell about 1000-1170px, 1px border. Top: dropdown, 3-step stepper, Pause, Start Over. Left code plus console, right event timeline drawing bars over gridlines. Or a right stepper with a 1px rail, dots and 19px labels. Plays automatically.

Board panel about 1320px, 60px gutters, soft shadow, dotted grid. Stickies, stamps, named cursors, a running timer and a spinning widget animate as rebuilt UI. It crosses the fold to invite scrolling.

Grid of 34-40px tiles with green checks and amber-outlined running jobs with counters, fading at the base. A floating white count card overlaps top right. Tiles change state one at a time, every 400ms.

spec: Black card up to 1260px, radius 28, centred 28px line and footage. Floating grey pill with a progress dash, five dots and a separate play or pause circle, docked in the card, parked below it on scroll.

110px disc inside two 1px concentric rings at about 200 and 296px, pastel chips sitting on the rings. Or arcs clipped by the cell bottom with a soft wedge sweeping round and one pill with a pulsing dot.
Full-bleed 320px band. 180px white cards, radius 4, slide left through a 4px vertical scan line: dashed wireframes before, finished UI with 32px check badges after. Loop seamlessly.

Pills above a real preview: active filled, content changes per value. Or a 664x404 panel, radius 24, with an image at left and five white mono pills at right, active tinted, each pill a real parameter name.

Frame 912x456, 2px white border, radius 0. Left panel grey boxes, right panel accent with white mono code. 1px divider, 32-44px white round handle with bracket glyph, mono caps corner labels. Auto-nudge once on enter.
Small working sample app beside a mono event table. New rows arrive tinted as the app is used, and a chart panel overlaps. Windows overlap with real shadows. The visitor generates the data.
Black code window, every line blurred except one, with that token highlighted and a floating type hover card in 14px mono with a hairline. The blur moves line to line, like a focus pull.
A sentence appears word by word on a rule with per-token numbers under it, a candidates list beside it, and a scrubber labelled 30x slowed down, from Detailed to Realtime.
Solid colour band. Five 197x268 tiles washed by the ground, centre tile 272x305 in full colour, raised with a shadow, 16px caption beneath. The wash cycles along the row.

Plan comparison table: 244 to 320px label column plus equal plan columns, 53 to 66px rows, 1px hairlines at 8% ink, 14px text. Header sticks under the nav and repeats plan, price and a small button per column. Mix ticks, dashes and short real values. Put a toggle or search in the corner cell.

Plan comparison split by 1px vertical hairlines only, no row rules. Rows pitch at 48px, 15px muted labels, 20px filled ink check circles, and a blank cell means no. Groups are 22px bold headings with a collapse chevron, and the rules break at each group. Calm for long feature lists with few text values.

Long comparison table with no rule between rows. One 1px hairline falls only between groups. Group titles 14px/500 in ink, children 14px/400 in muted ink, on about a 48px pitch, with 16px info icons trailing labels. Spacing alone carries the eye across columns, so it stays quiet at 80 or more rows.

Dark comparison matrix: 1px white rules at 6% on both axes, 230px label column, 70px rows, white ticks, and absence shown as a 5px grey dot, never a cross. 8px solid bands in a lifted tone split the groups, and column heads are 20px/600. Nothing reads as a failure.

Developer comparison in one bordered frame: tinted header with logo per column, mono caps group rows, 73px rows holding a 15px name and 13px note with inline code. 28px tinted status circles show yes, partial and no. Capped by a pill that shows the remaining rows, so the page stays short.

Compare hidden until asked for: sticky plan-name row with an 'Expand all' pill, then ten or so 53px category rows, each a 20px icon, 17px name and chevron on a 1px rule. Hover blackens one rule. Opening a row reveals its matrix. Use when the full table would run past 100 rows.

Comparison split by category tabs, because no reader needs every feature. A scrolling pill strip picks one product area, then a table of up to six 164px columns with right-aligned values, small ticks and crosses, a tinted group row and dotted rules inset per cell so column edges stay readable.

Comparison with one plan's column lifted by a full-height tone step: a 2 to 10% fill or side hairlines, 50 to 73px rows, header and cells in the same tint. Pair small multiplier pills on real values. No slab, no shadow. The tint must run unbroken from header to foot.

Own product against rivals: one solid accent column about 204px wide overshooting the rows by 30 to 40px top and bottom, white ring checks inside, rival column with pale crosses, 75px rows, row rules passing behind the slab. Works with two to three columns and ten rows at most.

Small rate table inside a dark feature cell: 1px grid, 48px rows, rivals in 12px grey. Your own row alone gets an accent frame, a dark tint of that accent, your logo and the winning number in full accent. Everything else stays grey, so the eye needs no reading.

Two columns or panels, no grid: 'before' muted with crosses or every line struck through, 'after' at full contrast with ticks or a keyline. 24px gap, 16 to 18px lines. Strikethrough does the disqualifying. Works as a qualifier too: who this is for, and who it is not for.

Cost difference shown as length: rival a full-width bar with its price, yours a 12px dot or a short bar. 12 to 32px bar height, 22px tabular prices right-aligned, a row of shared assumptions above and small-print method below. Use only with honest, sourced numbers.

Product pricing as a white card with rows: name and short description left, a tinted rate cell right, split by 1px dashed lines, 8px radius, soft shadow. Headline rate 16 to 18px, conditions 13px beneath. Reads like a bank's fee schedule. Right for usage fees that need sentences, not ticks.

Three to four equal cards compare approaches or formats: 10 to 12px radius, title 16px/600, facts in grey rows, the recommended card tinted. Simple and safe for consumer and education pages. Use when options differ in kind rather than feature by feature; avoid when a real table would be clearer.

A plain documentation table: 1px pale grid on every cell, tinted header, 14px bold, 27 to 48px rows, optional zebra, keyboard chips or short values. No plan marketing at all. Correct for specs, shortcuts, fees and lens options, where scanning a fact matters more than any impression.

A plain list replaces the table: tinted panel radius 28, centred 48px heading, then three text columns of 17/21 muted names, with small chevrons on those that link. For answering 'does it work with mine?' when the answer is a list of devices or models.

Three or four plans in one frame sharing 1px rules, no gaps, radius 0 to 8. 32px padding, 14px name, 48 to 56px price, muted one-line fit, then 'Everything in X, plus' list. Recommended cell is one tone brighter, with the only filled button. Use subgrid so rows align across plans.

Three to five separate plan cards, 1px line, no fill or a faint one, no shadow, gap 16 to 32, radius 4 to 24. 24 to 32px padding: name, 30 to 36px price, one-line fit, full-width button, then six to eight ticks at 30 to 36px pitch. Pick the recommended plan with a small tag.

Plan cards one tone step off the page, no border or shadow, or a 5% hairline, gap 8 to 10, radius 4 to 16, 16 to 24px padding. Every button is a grey pill except the recommended plan's, which is solid ink, so one filled button makes the choice. Feature lists grouped under small rules.

Four plan cards, 16px gap, 14px radius, 1px hairlines, with exactly one filled solid ink and its button flipped to white. Keep type and structure identical across cards. The inversion is the recommendation, so drop badges. Keep inverted on phones. Works from three to four plans.

Plans sit in one shell and the recommended column rises 16 to 32px above and below its neighbours, with a lighter fill or a 2px outline and a slightly larger title. No drop shadow is needed, because the broken top edge does the lifting. Three to five columns.

Featured plan gets no lift, no border, no badge. Only colour marks it: an accent mono label, a white filled pill where others are outlined, accent square bullets, brighter text. Other plans stay in grey. Quietest way to recommend, and strongest on dark ruled grids.

Pricing built as a product window: shell radius 16, padding 4, 44px title row, then four panes radius 12 in a lifted dark tone with 4px gutters. 20px name with muted audience note right, 30px price, one fee row, hairline, ticks pinned to the base. No per-plan button, no featured plan.

One 1024px sheet, 12px radius, soft shadow, holds all plans. Top strip carries a caps title and annual toggle, then three columns split by hairlines, then a tinted bottom strip with an upsell line. Plans read as a single document rather than competing cards.

Each plan column opens with a distinct tile, about 262 by 200px at radius 12 to 16, holding name and price or a mascot, art or black header block. Button under the tile, feature list open beneath it on the page with no card. One tile may carry a grain gradient to mark the pick.

One offer in one wide card, about 1088 by 426, radius 24, 1px warm line, soft tinted shadow. Left: small label, 40px name, 80px price with small unit, muted billing line, 50px full-width button. 1px vertical rule. Right: seven to nine ticks at 36px pitch.

One plan as a 416px card under a Yearly/Monthly pill: 16px item left, dotted leader, right-aligned 13px mono caps status, either included or a dated promise. Full-width 48px button below. Reads like a receipt, so the honest 'coming soon' line builds trust.

One price set as a sentence or a large figure with no plan grid: centred or left, 48 to 80px figure with small unit and the conditions at text size, a link or button below. For one product, one fee, a quote-based service or a set menu.

Two plan cards side by side, radius 10 to 20: a quiet free or basic card next to a filled or tinted paid card. Same bullet structure in both, 24 to 45px price, full-width button. Emphasis comes from fill and button alone. Use when only two offers exist.

Two 532 by 287 cards, 16px gap, 8px radius. Standard card: copy left, tinted rate panel right inset 4px. Custom card in dark ink: copy left, four stacked chips right inset 4px. Separates pay-as-you-go from talk-to-us without a tier table.

Prices as list rows, not cards: 14 to 15px label left, right-aligned bold price, 28 to 75px pitch, hairlines or none, inside the text column. Suits museum admission, service fees, or a small product's plans. Add a foot row linking to details. Tabular numerals, no icons.

Price set by the reader: slider with 1M, 10M and 50M ticks or an inline select per plan, boxed value, per-unit rate, and a bar reading 'Estimated total' with a button. Prices update live with no layout shift. For metered products where a flat tier table would mislead.

White or lifted plan cards on a saturated field or dark colour band, radius 16 to 24, 22px gaps, no highlighted tier needed because the field already gives the section its energy. Keep one colour plus white. Works for bold consumer and developer brands; avoid behind dense lists.

Plans as link tiles rather than tables: 24px radius, 24px padding, 24px name, 18px price, 16px muted line, one arrow bottom right, whole tile clickable. Three over two on a dark ground. For consumer accounts or packages where comparison happens on the next page.

Price as the hero object: four split-flap tiles about 200 by 128, radius 16, subtle dark gradient, thin numerals crossing an 8px split, flipping when a large text toggle switches monthly to yearly. One striking moment for a one-price product, never for a tier table.

FAQ as one reading column, 640 to 944px, centred or left aligned, heading aligned to it. Rows pitch 57 to 88px on 1px hairlines, 16px/500 to 600 questions, thin plus or chevron at far right, no cards, all collapsed. Answers 16px at 1.6 in muted ink, under 34em.

FAQ with heading alone in the left column and rows in the right half: 36 to 52px title top left, 56 to 75px rows, 1px rules top and bottom, 16 to 20px questions, 16px chevrons. Optional tone band behind. The empty left column gives a dull section its composure.

Split FAQ with one line drawing, photo or mascot under the title in the left column, 44 to 55px heading, rows right at 656px, 74px pitch, plus at right. A section band in brand colour is common. Art must belong to the brand, or leave the column empty.

FAQ rows as tone tiles, no rules: 56 to 80px tall, 8 to 12px gaps, radius 8 to 22, 16 to 20px question, thin plus or a 36px white disc holding a chevron. Open row expands within its own fill. Title left. A final 'Ask anything else' row can route to a person.

FAQ rows as outlined boxes: 1px line, radius 0 to 16, 58 to 120px tall, 12 to 24px gaps. A square toggle button at right, 36 to 44px, gives it a form-like, deliberate feel. Heavier than rules, so match it to a square, printed or industrial page.

FAQ numbered like an index: right-hand list about 52% wide, 68px rows, no dividers, grey 20px tabular index, 20px question, tiny chevron. Hover fills the whole row one tone at radius 6. Numbers state the length honestly and help on a sales call.

Questions set as large as section headings: 24 to 40px, 80 to 135px rows, 1px rules, thin plus or a filled disc. Hover or open fills the row or turns the type to accent. Makes a few FAQs read as statements. Six to ten short questions at most.

FAQ with a heavy control as the only strong object: 40px solid ink discs holding a thin white plus, 88px rows, 20px/600 questions, 1px rules, a heading row with a 56px button right. Controls that bold suit a soft page that needs a firm ending.

Rows with no visible dividers that come alive on hover: the hovered row lifts into a soft panel at radius 25, or fills one tone step across the full 1300px width. 20px questions at 61 to 112px pitch. Depends on hover, so keep a clear chevron for touch.

No accordion. Every answer open in a 670px left-aligned column: 22px display questions, 16/26 body, 34px between pairs, real links, a 20px hash anchor appearing in the left margin on hover. Searchable with cmd-F and linkable. Needs answers worth reading and suits developer tools.

Master and detail: question list left, one answer pane right. Active row lighter, pane echoes the question and answers in a chat bubble or sand panel with small pagination. Shell radius 32 with 16px inset panes. Eight questions at most. Needs a stacked accordion on phones.

Long FAQs split by topic: a left rail of 24px category names beside 853px rows at 81px pitch, or tabs above a 640px column, or two audience-named columns. Each group keeps the same row. Answers 'which part applies to me' before anyone reads a question.

Two 610px columns of 44 to 48px rows, 16px/700 questions, 12px chevrons, ten questions visible at once. No panels or shading. Compact, for a FAQ that must not take a whole screen. Answers push only their own column, so keep them short.

Dense disclosure rows for details, not persuasion: 40 to 48px tall, 14px labels, 1px rules, plus or chevron at right. Use under a product buy box, on visit pages, or for 17 or more questions where density signals candour. Upper-case or mono labels suit stores.

The whole FAQ sits in one tinted or white sheet, 710 to 900px, radius 10 to 16, 48px padding, 70px rows on hairlines, chevrons in 24px discs that darken when open. Reads as a reference area. Use it when the page behind is busy or dark.

FAQ and final ask share one screen: left column 64/64 closing heading and pill, right a 498px stack of 60px rows, radius 8, 12px gap. Saves a section on short pages and keeps the button beside the last doubt it answers.

Page ends on its own ground: no panel, gradient or image, 130 to 230px padding above and below. Centred 48 to 72px two-line sentence, tight leading, one filled and one quiet 44px pill, 12px apart. The only centred block on a left-aligned page, so the change of axis signals the end.

No band or fill. Heading left, 36 to 56px over two lines, with one sentence and a 48px button in a right column, or the buttons alone on the same line. Under a hairline, about 120px padding. Confidence comes from size. Suits calm finance and SaaS pages.

Close framed by the page's rails: a 190 to 415px band between two full-bleed hairlines, no colour change, where side rails stop. 34 to 64px line left or centred, two 42 to 44px pills. Needs a visible rule system earlier on the page, or it reads as empty.

The button is the design: centred 64 to 80px headline, muted line, then a 64 to 72px button, radius 18 to 20, 24 to 32px bold label, or a giant 750px pill holding the whole line. Add ratings or a checklist beneath. Say one thing.

The end rhymes with the start: repeat the hero mark, panel, icon shape or slogan at a new scale. A 590px faded squircle echoing the app icon, a ghost logo bleeding off a corner, or the hero stack again. Quiet, and needs no new art.

Inset panel one tone off the page, radius 6 to 42, 24 to 32px page inset, 320 to 460px tall. 48 to 52px heading left or centred, filled and outlined buttons. Optional blurred bloom in two hues on the right half, kept pale, never behind the text.

One inset panel in full brand colour or dark ink, 1248 to 1376px, radius 12 to 20, 48 to 72px heading, two buttons. It works only if it is the one saturated surface on the page. Add one owned detail: a drawn line, a notch, a pattern.

Tinted inset panel, about 282 to 450px tall, radius 24, carrying a brand pattern with the centre cleared for text: 1px rings radiating from the button, pixel blocks at both sides, contour lines. 32 to 64px heading. The pattern rewards attention without competing with it.

Full-bleed colour band, 230 to 540px, centred 40 to 56px heading, 96px padding, one or two 48px buttons. Plain and common, the fallback of template pages. Lift it with a two-tone heading or a flat line drawing, and let it butt onto the footer.

Dark or white field with soft colour pooled at its edges: glows high behind a centred app icon, or blooms in the bottom corners, 40 to 64px heading on clean ground, one 48px button. Text never sits on the brightest area. Flows into the footer without a seam.

Closing on a real photograph or film: full bleed or a 1376px card at radius 32, 48 to 120px white heading placed in the image's own shadow, 16 to 22px copy, one white pill. Use a local scrim. Repeat the hero's world so the page closes a loop.

Half photo, half flat panel: 1360 by 450, radius 8 to 24, warm image beside a 48px heading, small eyebrow and a full-width 48px button pinned to the base. Or a 270px flush photo on the right of a dark card. Safe for health, retail and culture.

A 540px left-aligned card of dark grain lit from one side, radius 12, white mark, 36/39 heading, small white button. The right half of the row stays empty, so the close reads as a placed object rather than a band. Sits just above a matching dark footer.

Display type carries the ending: 100 to 250px flush left, leading under 1, a last word in accent or underlined, install block or field small beside it. On a black band or field. Keep a sharp scale contrast with something tiny next to it.

The close is a stack of links, not a band. Up to 110px lines filling the width, each with a thin chevron flush right, or 52px bar buttons with mono caps, or a 68px strip of numbered links. Navigation becomes type. Use when several next steps are equal.

End by routing, not by shouting: heading left, then two or three cards or rows, one per next step, each with title, one line and a 44 to 60px arrow disc. Radius 12 on a tinted panel at radius 24. Two-audience pages use two equal columns.

The last call to action is the product: centred 48px heading, then a real 54 to 62px input, up to 766px wide, radius 14, with its action inside. Prompt box, URL field, file drop or preset amounts. Starts the first task instead of describing it.

The close is the download itself: OS columns of chips split by 1px rules, a copyable install command beside a docs button, or a QR card with store ratings for desktop visitors. Real commands, real platforms. Nothing to read, one thing to do.

Heading and buttons left, a working piece of the product right: a status stack, a fan of app screens, devices on a reflective floor, an editor crop flush to the edge. Clipped by the panel. Must be current product, not a stock mock.

The close physically joins the footer: the page plate, inset 52px from one side, ends in a 50px corner and reveals colour beneath, or a white card straddles the seam, or the footer overlaps a grain band. Depth with no shadow, and the page reads as one object.

Centred 48 to 64px heading in a clear middle, ringed by scattered objects: 68px logo tiles, framed photos at differing sizes, pixel sprites. A grainy glow rising through the lower third can tint the ones it touches. Objects must be real integrations, products or people.

Personality closes the page: a mascot rising from the panel's edge, a full cast lined up on the footer, a straight-faced parody of sales tactics that still converts. 60px heading, one button. Only for brands already that voice. Never on health, law or finance.

One owned drawing fills half the band: extruded ribbons, a dithered ASCII tree, a chrome wordmark, overlapping lens circles, tilted slab. Heading and pill on the other side. It must be made for this brand and appear earlier on the page, or it reads as decoration.

The contact detail is the headline: a 48px phone number on a 90px strip, or a 76px email address in the page's display type, with no button. For agencies, local trades and voice products, where one action really is a call or an email.

A 60 to 66px bar docked to the viewport base with 8px inset: 14px bold label, price or avatar stack, one 48px pill. Stays through all scrolling. Use for one strong consumer offer, never with a chat bubble or cookie bar competing for the same edge.

Email field as a single line: 1 to 1.5px underline, 12 to 16px placeholder, submit as plain text at the far end of the same line or a small block abutting it, 11px consent below. No box. 360 to 580px wide. Works on photos and dark blocks.

Sign-up as one ruled row across the page: a 32px sentence on a 2px rule, 908px wide, then 20px on, a 444px email field sitting on the same rule, with plain Submit text at the right. No box and no button. Reads as a line in a magazine.

Heading, one line of copy, then a 40 to 48px field and a separate button side by side, 8 to 12px apart, 385 to 540px total, often centred. Correct and invisible. Lift it with a line of real proof or a joke in the copy.

Button lives inside the field: 50 to 62px capsule or 52px square outline, inset 4 to 8px, 16px placeholder, button or arrow seated inside. Button height equals field height minus twice the inset, and inner radius equals outer minus inset. Reads as one object.

Email field as a flat tone with no border, radius or visible button: 30 to 60px tall, grey fill two to four steps off the page, small caps placeholder. Suits fashion, galleries and luxury. Keep a keyboard submit and a visible label.

The field is the section: 64 to 67px tall, up to 683px wide, 42px placeholder or a mono placeholder that keeps the developer voice, submit at right or a 64px button beside it, on a grey or flat colour band.

No field on the page: a label, one sentence and a Subscribe pill or text link, about 120px tall, following the page grid like any other section. Or one huge staggered link. Sign-up moves to its own page, so the page stays in its own voice.

Row inside the footer between two 1px rules at 8%: 20/600 title and 15px line left, 48px outlined input about 330px wide plus button right, 13px consent below. Button stays grey until the field has content. Quiet, and always reachable.

Sign-up on a photograph: full-bleed band or a card at radius 32 with 7px margin, 44px headline, 62px white field, 48px pill, on the calm side of a warm portrait. Check text against the busiest pixel; a busy image defeats it.

Half real photograph, half flat panel in brand colour: heading, one line, email field and button. Bands 260 to 400px tall. Good for food, culture and hospitality, where the picture is the reason to subscribe.

Full-width flat colour band with a sign-up heading left and small free-text copy right, little else. Works as a page-level colour moment for a culture listing or daily product. Keep to one colour and white.

An owned illustration gives the sign-up a character: a pixel mascot in an envelope, a spot drawing on a pale panel, art dissolving into the form's ground. 32 to 36px bold heading, a caption saying how often it arrives, underline or 42px input. The drawing is the reason to look.

Centred 54px heading and 50px input, with product renders floating around: sharp near the top, one large and blurred in front for depth, or a generated torn shape behind. Peach or brand gradient rising from one corner. Needs real rendered objects.

Centred 440 to 600px modal over a dimmed page, half lifestyle photo, half form with a discount headline, one field, black button and an underlined decline link. It interrupts on arrival, so delay it, offer real value and keep close obvious. Stores only.

Persistent small cue instead of a modal: a 40 by 240px rotated tab on the right edge, a 214 by 48px corner tab, or a 60px bottom bar with a close x. Never covers a photo's subject and stays reachable.

Small card holding the sign-up inside a grid or sidebar: 300 to 500px, 12 to 24px radius, title, one line, field or button, sitting in the same slot as a quote or article. Joins the page's rhythm instead of interrupting it.

Two fields stacked in one container: 460px wide, radius 24, 2px spectral or thin outline, 13px labels above 18px placeholders, split by a hairline, then a full-width 52px pill. For private betas and waitlists, where asking a role is worth it.

Sales contact split: left 64px headline, 18px muted line, then logos with one stat each. Right 568px form on the bare page: 14/500 labels, 38px inputs, radius 6, 1px line, 2-up rows at 16px gap, 26px between groups, 150px textarea, pill submit, 12px consent. Proof sits beside the ask.

Fields are single lines: 1px bottom rule, 12px labels above or inside, 16px light values, 56px or more between rows, 2-up on desktop. A large 60 to 90px title left. Rule turns full ink on focus. Pill or block submit. For studios, hospitality and portfolios.

Form in one tinted panel, 8px radius, 24px padding: 16/600 labels with muted asterisks, 42px white square-cornered inputs, 1px grey line, 16px gutters, 42px dark button bottom left with an arrow. Or a slate panel with a neon submit. Reads as one task.

Long form split into steps: a 540 to 608px card or column, two to four fields per step, 'Step 1 of 2' caption or numbered tabs, full-width 46px Next. First step asks only email and one qualifier. Filled 58px fields with labels inside, or inline labels.

Contact as a conversation: a phone-like sheet with a handle and avatar, one question at a time in 16px, ghost answer, circular arrow. Email address with a Copy pill beside it for people who prefer to write. For agencies and AI products.

The form is replaced by a calendar: 874px white scheduler radius 8 with host and agenda pane, month grid and time buttons, on a full-bleed brand colour under a 60px centred headline. One step closer to the meeting than a message.

Dark or coloured band: left 48 to 64px headline, 18px copy, three tick lines saying what happens next. Right a 517px white card, radius 16 to 28, 46px inputs, 50px accent submit. An offset colour slab behind the card can give it weight.

Form card placed over a 3D scene, photo or blurred image: 330 to 500px, radius 8 to 20, small labels, stacked fields. Legible only with a solid or strong frosted card. Works when the art is the brand and the form short.

No form: a sentence with two underlined links, big labelled emails, a phone number, or offices beside a photograph. For portfolios, studios, restaurants and dentists, where a human answers and the fastest route is a call or an email.

Before any field, route the visitor: 48px heading left, right column of four rows on near-ink 1px rules, each a 22px title with arrow and a 14px line. Mono links below the heading for the rest. Sends sales, support and partners to different places.

Default stacked form: 44px white fields, radius 4, 1px line, 12px labels above, a dropdown, a checkbox, a dark button. Correct and anonymous. Use it for institutions, and spend effort on field count, error text and what happens next.

For a physical place, contact is directions: a map with brand-coloured pins beside a colour panel with a 51px 'Directions' heading, a journey-planner button and collapsible rows for tube, bus and parking on underline rules.

One 1px outline split into 4 to 12 cells by shared rules, no gaps, no radius. Each cell: 11px mono index, 15px/500 title, 14px muted copy, then a proof row pinned low showing a different tiny real artefact per cell. Optional + marks on junctions. Last cell tinted, closing with a link.

Three to six open columns, 24 to 32px gutters, no boxes. Each opens with a 1px top rule, or left rule with 32px inset, then 28px of space, a small icon or number, a 20 to 24px/400 title and 16 to 17px copy at 1.6. One line replaces the whole card.

Three or four columns with no boxes: 20 to 24px line icon, 16 to 20px title, 15 to 16px grey copy, aligned to the heading's left edge. Best with a bold run-in lead continuing into grey text. For six to twelve small capabilities, never the page's main feature section.

Four 270px columns on dashed vertical guides that run the full page through band changes. A 1px by 16px accent tick hangs on the guide beside each 15px/600 title, over a 40px duotone spot icon, 15/24 copy and inline 500-weight accent links. Needs guides across several sections.

Three to five columns with no icons. Hold one small device: a tracked accent code over a 36/46 heading, a first letter in the accent, or chips under each paragraph. 18/30 body. Hover can turn one cell into a surface. Needs specific copy, because nothing hides a vague sentence.

Three columns split by 1px rules at 8% ink, no cards. 11px mono figure label at 30% ink, one custom line drawing about 240 to 320px, 15px title, 15/24 muted copy. Faces filled with page colour so nearer planes hide farther lines, brightness falling downward. Needs real drawings.

Two or three hairline cells, each a 20px/600 column head over five to eight 18/34 rows with an 18px check. No icons, no blurbs. Reads as a contract you can count. Variant: a two-column grid of 150 by 38 outlined chips beside a statement card.

Three or four columns, 8 to 32px gaps. A plate 286 to 500px tall holding a real fragment or photo cropped by its edge, then 24px of space, a 20 to 28px/400 title and 16/1.4 copy at 58% ink on the bare page. No card, border or shadow behind the text.

Two to five candid photo cards about 421 by 500px, 16 to 24px gaps, radius 8 to 16. Translucent 11px caps pill top left, 24 to 28px title and one line with a bold lead at the foot, 40px white circle arrow. Scrim only in the lower half, 0.8 at base.

Two tiles per row, 8 to 16px gaps, near full bleed, little or no radius. Centred stack in the top third: 40/44 title, one line, pills or chevron links. Product fills the lower 55 to 60%, art-directed per tile, some cropped at the base. Pair a light tile with a dark one.

Borderless trays a tint 2 to 4% off the page, radius 12 to 16. Title and short copy on top, a different real UI fragment rising from the base, cropped or fading into the tray. Fragment changes per card, frame stays fixed. Rows may mix one full-width with two half-width.

Image, title and text inside one card: radius 8 to 24, 1px border or soft fill, media inset 16 to 20px with a slightly smaller radius, 20px title, 15px copy, link pinned to the base. Correct for articles, courses and resources. Prefer bare plates for product features.

Radius 8 to 16, 1px border at 8% ink, no fill, no shadow, 24px padding, 16 to 24px gap, 20px icon, 16 to 20px title. Good for link indexes and docs hubs where boxes signal a click. Change one thing, such as a pinned low title or a solid closing tile.

Borderless cards one step off the page, radius 8 to 40, gap 8 to 16. A 64px white icon tile, a claim, detail pushed low. Suits small claims on a tinted band. White cards on a saturated flood is the bold form. Avoid three equal cards with one sentence each.

Rows of two tiles in a 2:3 ratio, about 522 and 776px, swapping sides each row, radius 20, gap 24, tops offset 12px on purpose. A tint per tile, a demo filling the top 60 to 70%, then a 38 to 40px title and 19 to 20px copy.

Cards 304 to 400px wide at a 20 to 22px gap run past the right edge, the last cut by the viewport as the scroll cue. 36 to 40px round prev and next controls, disabled at 50%. For eight or more parallel items that need not all be read.

A table of contents: rows about 70px tall on 1px rules, a 44px light name left, a one-line description starting 62% across, no icons or cards. Hover shifts the row 12px and darkens the copy. For studios and services with five or more real items.

Short wide link tiles about 434 by 78px, 8 to 20px gaps, 24px label left, small illustration or product cutout and chevron right, under one plain question. Hover darkens the fill one step. Sorts visitors by need rather than feature. Good high on multi-audience pages.

One composed moment instead of a list: three hairline circles with captions in each lobe, a centred pitch between four corner cards, or columns stepping 32 to 216px lower. Use once per page, only when the content has that real structure, or the offset looks like a mistake.

Full-bleed tinted band or rounded panel: four columns of 36px line icon, 16px/600 title and 12 to 14px centred line. For shipping, returns, hours and amenities on stores and local businesses, low on the page. Keep it small, because it holds no argument.

A 440px copy column beside a 555 by 386px stage, radius 20 to 28, 1px inset hairline, tint changing per row. Layer two or three real fragments, one cut by the stage edge. 30/38 heading, 16/24 body at 60% ink, one text link. Rows may sit in alternating 590px bands.

One 1232px card per row, 6 to 18px radius, 1px hairline, rows 12px apart. Left: 22px title, 16px body, button pinned low. Right: 584px pane one tint off with layered UI cropped by the card. Keep copy on one side. A gradient hairline appears on the hovered row.

Two equal columns, plate 460 to 570px tall with a window cropped at its base, copy pinned to the plate's base line and the column above left empty. Two-tone heading, muted line then full ink, 16px at 56% ink. Next row flips 120px below. Needs visible page rails.

A 265 to 360px copy column beside an 830px window or photo that passes the container and runs off the viewport edge, saying there is more. Add four 70px-pitch icon rows for spec detail. Use once or twice for the most important product moment.

evidence.name: Medusa622: Luxury Skin & Nails in Knightsbridge

spec: Paired tiles 16px apart, radius 15, ratios changing per row, such as 778 and 582, then 545 and 817. Flat grey text tile, 25px padding, 32px heading, 17/29 body weighted low. Overlap rows by up to 180px for more movement. A zigzag with the stiffness removed.

Panels about 1312 by 670px, radius 30 to 40, gap 24 to 40, each a two or three stop pastel wash or flat flavour colour. A 48px heading with a small tag on one side, one floating UI card or tall photo on the other. Four panels at most.

Near viewport-tall 50/50 split, butted with no gap: full-bleed photo beside a flat field sampled from it. Small caps label, 26 to 32px title, 15/24 copy, thin outlined button. Change the colour per row. Print-like, for hospitality, architecture, food and institutions.

Consecutive 100vh sections, no dividers. A 430px text block sits in the empty part of each photo at a 100px margin, moving per shot: 48px heading, three lines of 16px, one ghost button. Needs at least three strong images. Flat colour scenes around one object also work.

Image 56 to 62% wide beside 320 to 420px text, about 100 to 130px between rows, sides swapping. Better when the 767px photo shifts sideways by 280px instead of fully swapping. Muted 15/21 body, 11px caps link with a 50px underline. Depends entirely on the photography.

A 369px copy column doing real work beside an 831px plate: heading, short copy, then three 46px plus-rows on hairlines, a two-column checklist with 24px filled circles, or four ruled spec rows, ending in stacked buttons. For rows with several facts.

Print-style size contrast: a 60px centred headline over a 212 by 286px portrait with 200px of white after it, or small photos scattered at different sizes beside a 52px heading. The image is far narrower than the type. For fashion, hospitality and magazines.

The reader does the demonstrating: a before and after slider with a draggable handle over one image, or a row of six 40px colour swatches that swap a name, story and buy button. Only worth it when the change is visible at a glance.

Three to six pills 38 to 56px tall, 8 to 16px gap, 16 to 28px above a window at real size. Active is solid ink, or a 1px ink outline on quiet pages. The window is taller than the section and cut by its bottom rule. Optional dimmed neighbour panels at 25%.

Indicator on a 1px rule above each label, filling as a 5 to 8 second timer; label never moves. Active full ink, others 50%. Pause on hover and focus, stop under reduced motion. Variants: ring timer in a corner, arc on the active row, foot segments on a slide.

A 628px stage, radius 20, beside a 518px accordion on 1px hairlines: 24px titles, 20/30 dark grey body, 24px circular chevrons, a 72px ink segment on the open row's top rule. Height animates via grid-template-rows. Fix the stage height. Best tab form for phones.

The list is the design: names 28 to 100px on 1px rules or none, active full ink, others 25 to 55%, a small preview swapping beside the list. A progress line can fill the active rule. For services and channels with good names, in agency and bold brand pages.

Three or four rows left, the active wrapped in a white 12px-radius card with a 1px border, others grey on the page, a live preview right. Or a 500px dark rail with a 2px white bar and blurb beside a chart. Compact, like an interface in the page.

14 to 18px labels, 24 to 40px gaps, on a full-width 1px rule, active indicator 2 to 4px. Sits directly on the window it controls. Placing the bar on top of the rule with the label below looks more considered than an underline. Scrolls sideways on phones.

A pale track pill about 56px tall with a solid active pill 6px inside, 17px labels, or a 404 by 46 rail with tracked mono caps. For two to five short options such as device or audience. Can pin under the nav while tiles scroll beneath.

Three tabs about 346 to 389px wide and 90 to 113px tall, radius 8 to 16, 1px border, 40px icon, 14 to 16px label, one description line. Active gets an accent border or thin glow on its bottom edge, 32px above a full dashboard.

Bordered 13 to 14px mono tabs on the top of the frame, active tab white with a 2px accent underline, content panel below holding a command or code. Honest for developer docs. Variants: square nodes on active corners, or flush filled cells about 226 by 46px.

One slide per view, 504 to 1140px wide, with the next peeking 36 to 40px away. Round arrows aligned to the heading, or a transport row with play ring and progress dashes that treats the carousel as media. For a few rich slides.

The control sits on a full-bleed image: three 42px pills bottom centre, active solid white, others with a 2px white outline, or a 14px list bottom left on a 30px rhythm with a small vertical tick. For products or card types.

Five tall panels about 300 by 400px bleeding off the right edge, photos duotoned to one hue so they match, 1px separators, a 40px circle plus top left, 20/500 white label at the foot. The active panel lifts its label 22px. For audiences or products.

The control is part of the idea: a heading written as a sentence with underlined variables and option lists either side of a stacked card deck, or hairlines running from each option into an illustration that fills to match. Use once, when the content has real structure.
Text or small pills, 13 to 18px, directly above a grid of cards, active in the accent, no underline, 28px gaps. Filters rather than swaps. For logos, customer stories and shop categories.

A 444 to 672px list beside a sticky 584 to 800px stage, three to five steps at about 72vh each. Scroll sets the active step, time plays the change. Active full ink, others 30%, plus one bar or rule. Stage must stay full. Plain flow without JavaScript.

A 218 to 348px sticky index beside a 1000px scrolling column, four to six chapters. 14 to 18px labels, active near-black with a 2px tick on the page rail. Each chapter is a run-in statement over a same-inset demo cell. Becomes a sticky horizontal row on phones.

A pinned screen with a fixed skeleton where only contents change across three to seven chapters: a 100vh film with a foot caption on the emptier side, a shared rule, a time rail of ticks, or a stage flooded per product beside an 88px icon rail.

Sheets about 1248 by 560px, radius 16, sticky at a top offset growing 14px per sheet so edges peek, shadow 0 30px 40px at 28% black. 72px left padding, 48px title, 20/30 copy, UI with a dark rail bleeding off the right. Three to six peers, block flow.

A 50/50 split: one half pins a panel or photo with copy at its foot while the other scrolls macro, model and detail shots, or rows on 1px rules that swap the pinned photo. Fill can step lighter per image. For one product or person with several images.

A 1px vertical line through the content with a marker tracking scroll: at page centre with copy left and UI right, or at page left with a 10px node per row turning into an accent ring. Inactive rows dim to 40%. Nothing pins, which keeps it light.

Type as the event, once per page: a pinned pale section where three 64px lines arrive from 8px blur and low opacity above three 70px step cards, or a 3D form inside a ring of 120 ticks filling with progress. For a positioning statement.

Vertical scroll drives panels sideways: a pinned heading over four 110px segment bars filling with progress, while photo and bullet panels slide in from the right over a dot grid. For parallel items rather than ordered steps.

A rounded card holding a headline and screenshot scales up until it fills the viewport as you scroll. One per page, as an entrance to something important. A plain scale without a crop change looks like a zoom bug.

Three or four columns, each a small marker, a 32px tight title, 18/29 copy, then the real screen at full size with no window chrome: a picker, a form, a feed. Reserve copy height so the proofs start level. The first thing to try for any product.

A centred 720px column of 28px solid ink circles with 13px numerals joined by a 1px line, 24px/400 titles indented 56px, 17/27 body, 150px pitch. Needs no art, so it suits services and local businesses. The line stops at the last dot.

Three to five centred columns on a 1px line running dot centre to dot centre: 16px hollow dots, current one solid, 11px mono index, 16px/600 title, 14px caption. Clicking a stop can swap a panel below, so it doubles as tabs. For lifecycles, APIs and finance.

Rows about 140px apart on 1px rules beside a sticky heading: 14px mono numeral, 24px title, 16px line, small link with a long arrow. Or numerals hung in the margin so alignment is the only ornament. For short, numerous steps.

Three to five columns split or topped by 1px rules, 28px inner padding, 12 to 13px label, 20 to 24px step name, 16/25 copy. One signature: a giant letter per column spelling the method, 64px outlined numerals, or a meter filling by thirds. For agency and B2B process.

A stepper: a 56px numeral beside a 560px white card, others collapsed and grey, opposite one coloured tile or floating UI card that changes per step, with progress dots. Can autoplay. For when one phone or card can show each stage.

The route becomes the picture: a sine path drawn on scroll with stops and a floating detail card, role cards seated on a thick ring, or light travelling an open outline. Use only when the process has a real shape and you have strong drawings.

Three cards about 330 to 390px, rotated plus or minus 3 to 5 degrees, slightly overlapping, soft 40px shadow, hand-drawn arrows between. Number and title on top, copy pinned low. Human and handmade, for freelancers and small brands. Once per page.

For developers, steps are code: a bracketed mono number, 16px/600 title and 16/28 prose beside a 545px code card aligned at the top, or three 328px panes showing a transformation. The layout itself explains the process.

One step per viewport: a numeral of about 300px with a 1px metallic stroke and faint fill tucked behind a 640px phone, copy low and right at 24px with 18px grey. For a slow premium story of three steps.

When steps are days: three rows split by 1px rules, a 24px light date with a small chip in the first column, a bare 16/24 list in the second. Or centred date and description pairs with no rails. For events, courses and launches.
Steps as coloured sheets, radius 16, overlapping upward on scroll beside a sticky heading, 36px titles with numbers and 18px body. Reuse the sticky stacked-sheets recipe. Three to five steps.

Three or four equal cards each with a number, a title and a line. The template, and the lowest-scoring steps form. Use only when steps are trivial on a small local page. Prefer a vertical numbered rail, which needs no art and looks considered.

evidence.name: Brand Designer for B2B SaaS, Fintech & Tech Startups

spec: Logo alone top-left, left third otherwise empty, link columns starting at about 33 percent of the width on a 200-230px pitch. 14px heads, 14px muted links on 28-31px rows. One short legal row about 100px below. Nothing else: no tagline, no socials row, no newsletter.

Four to seven equal columns across the whole container, no logo column, 14/500 heads, 14px muted links on 28px rows, on the page ground or one flat tone. Extra groups stack under short columns so the base stays level. A small status, theme or legal row closes it.

The densest thing on an airy page: 12px throughout in a narrow 980px column, bold group heads, about 26px pitch, five columns of stacked groups, hairlines top and bottom, numbered notes above, pipe-divided legal row below. Collapses to ruled accordion rows on phones. Hundreds of links stay calm.

Left block of about 300-430px holds logo, a two-line blurb and real proof: compliance marks, a live status dot, theme switch. Three to five link columns right, with small mono or muted heads, 14-16px links on 30-36px rows. Status line sits in the bottom row with a small green dot.

Signup is the first thing in the footer. Left block: 30px invitation, an honest line about what arrives, 42-48px field or one outlined Subscribe. Columns right from about 36 percent. Or a top row with title left and field right, a hairline, then columns. Never a field alone with no reason given.

The footer keeps the page's own grid: columns sit on the same guides or rails, split by 1px rules or dashed verticals that run through from above. Heads and links only, no fill change or a flat tone. Lines must meet the page edges. Works as a literal ruled table of 52px cells.

The white page ends in 24-40px bottom corners and lifts off a dark footer behind it, so the page reads as a sheet. The dark must sit behind the sheet, on body, or the corners show white. Six or seven columns of 14px links in the dark.

The footer is a dark or brand card inset 16-30px from the viewport on all sides, radius 8-24, about 1392 by 430 at a 1440 canvas. Columns pack to the right, wordmark bottom-left, the left two-thirds left empty on purpose. The page ground stays visible around it.

One full-bleed field of the brand colour, the largest flat colour on the page, held back until the end. All text in one tint of that field: white, or a dark of the same hue. Serif or display heads, 13-14px links, one lighter rule inset 16px. No second colour.

Links on top, then the wordmark at full container width as the very last thing, 220-380px tall, in full contrast, framed by hairlines. Use a trimmed SVG or size from ink bounds so it meets both margins exactly. Never stretch glyphs. Only a thin legal row may follow.

A very large wordmark set barely off the ground, about 4-8 percent of ink, and cropped by the page bottom or a hairline. It gives the footer weight without volume. Links stay in full contrast above it. Letters must fill the width, and the crop must look deliberate, cutting about a third.

evidence.name: Medusa622: Luxury Skin & Nails in Knightsbridge

spec: Edge-to-edge wordmark used as a window: halftone photo, moving video or customer imagery shows through the letters, or the letters are 1-1.5px outline with no fill. Use background-clip text or an SVG mask. The image must be busy enough to keep the letters readable at a glance.

evidence.name: Airpost: The Frontier Marketing OS for Frontier Companies

spec: The footer's largest element is a sentence, 76-170px, not a logo: a mission line, a repeat of the hero heading, or a plain ask. Small link columns or one legal row sit around it. Say something true and specific, or it reads as a slogan.

For studios and trades: no sitemap. Name, a labelled email and phone, address and social sit as text clusters on one ruled strip about 95px tall, or as label and value pairs at the left margin. Everything is selectable text, 15/20. Works at any size, up to a 70px address.

For anywhere people visit: phone, address and real opening hours are in the footer as text, not behind a link. Crest or script logo left, hours in three lines right, one row of links, thin rule, credit line. Say what is true: closed days, seasonal hours, separate kitchen times.

For few pages or a single funnel: one row under a hairline, about 60-110px tall, 12-14px. Copyright left, three links, status or socials right. Or a single centred sentence with dot separators. A short footer is honest. Padding it with columns of links that do not exist is what cheapens it.

A drawn or generated scene is the last image, cropped by the footer's top rule: a heap of mascots, a canvas ridge of hairlines, a horizon glow. Ordinary link columns sit below or over it. The scene must come from the brand's own world and stay under about 300px.

No separate block. The last photo or film runs to the page bottom and the footer is one row laid inside it: 12px tracked links, a round back-to-top, copyright right. The page ends on a picture. Needs a dark, quiet lower edge in the image, or a scrim drawn from it.

For regulated work, fine print gets a real layout: a 13px label in the left column, numbered notes in a 680px measure at 13/17 or 12/18, underlined links, bold run-ins on warnings, a one-step tint behind. Treat it as a document that someone will read.

Few links, set large: 20px rows on a 37px pitch, or 38-120px words stacked and right-aligned, sometimes numbered 01 to 06 with hairlines between. Type does the work, so no column heads. Only for sites with six to ten destinations.

Sitemap collapsed into ruled rows: 42-57px pitch, 15px labels, chevron or plus far right, 1px rules, in one column to the right or left of a form. Everything stays one tap away on phones, and the desktop page stops with calm. Hovered row turns full contrast.

The ending is one small made thing rather than a block: a tilted paper wall label, a desktop dock, a signature, a sticker back-link. Everything legally required lives inside the object. For personal sites and strong concepts only, once.

Left card about 310-430px holds what the app is for: QR tile, a phone crop, a rating with its review count. Three link columns to its right. The QR gives desktop visitors a real route to their phone. Only when the app is the main product.

Two or three uniform columns of square-cornered images with one caption row 8-12px below: name in ink, muted place or discipline, year, and a link or arrow right-aligned to the image edge. Gaps 16-24, no card, no border. The caption shares the image's left and right edges.

Rows change count on purpose: one full tile, then two, then three, all locked to the same gutters. Square corners, 20-50px gaps, 55px page margin or less. No hover chrome. The change of beat replaces any need for cards, and it looks curated rather than generated.

Title inside the image, bottom-left, inset 16-26px, on a scrim of about 80px rising from the base only. Tiles 16:9 or square, 0-8px radius, 8-24px gaps. Use when photographs are strong and dark enough at the foot. Never a flat overlay across the whole image.

One large tile beside a stack of smaller ones, with spans that vary row to row: 2+1+1 then 1+2+1 on four columns, deliberate holes allowed. 4-8px gaps, one small caption per tile. Different image scales give the eye a hierarchy that a uniform grid cannot.

Each work keeps its own proportions, uncropped. Set a max width per column, align the images to the bottom of the row so tops stagger and titles share one baseline, or centre them on the row midline. For art, architecture and anything where a crop would be a lie.

Edge to edge, 0-10px gaps, no captions, four to nine columns, and the page is simply the work. Fills the viewport so scale itself is the statement. Works for archives, community output and templates. Add a fade at the base if the wall is truncated, with one button on it.

Left-aligned to the page, running off the right edge with the next tile cut by the viewport: tiles 300-820px wide, radius 0-20, gap 16-20. A 21px caption under each, 36px round arrows below or above right. Native scroll with snap on touch. The peek is the affordance.

One slide about 930-1200px centred under the title, neighbours peeking both sides with a 12-16px gap. Below, a dot pager with an elongated progress dot and a small play-pause disc. Autoplay must have a pause control. For film, footage and big product pictures.

evidence.name: Alessandro Stella, Art Direction & Design Consultancy

spec: A horizontal band where every image has one fixed height and its own native width: 620px tall, widths 300-900, 100px gaps, white above and below. Driven by wheel or drag. Height is the only constant, so mixed work sits together without a crop.

Each project is one row under a 1px rule: large image left, short description mid, name right-aligned at far right, category on the row's bottom edge. Title stays top aligned beside tall media. Zones repeat exactly, so work of different shapes reads as one index.

The whole portfolio as a table: 40px rows, 14px text, columns title, type, client, year right-aligned, 1px rules, full width, no images until hover. Hovered row inverts to ink on ground and indents 14px. Reads as confidence: there is so much work that it needs a table.

A wide image with a narrow text column beside it, bottom-aligned: 920px photo plus 260px text, or an index of numbered titles beside one tall image. Rows may alternate. Label 11px, name 16px, body 14/1.6, arrow link. Row gap about 100px. Reads like a catalogue page.

One viewport holds one project; scroll swaps it in place. A centred 500-1170px frame stays pinned while neighbours enter from the edges, or a smaller clip rises over a large frame. Keep the swap under one screen of scroll, and give phones a plain stacked version.

Every project in one narrow column on the centre axis or a rail, images at natural ratio about 434-580px wide, 26-120px apart, no sections or headings. Name and place in a small column beside each. The length of the list is the proof.

Mixed sizes placed by hand across a loose grid, with lots of empty page: some cut-outs, some rectangles, each with a small mono number at its corner and one legend mapping numbers to names. Offsets of 40-120px. Needs real variety in the pictures.

Full-bleed row of about 320x240 photos at radius 12, each tilted about 2 degrees alternately, 35px gap, drifting slowly sideways, cut by both edges. One human moment on a technical page, or a hotel's scrapbook. Tilt under 3 degrees, and honour reduced motion.

Each project gets one thin horizontal slice of an image, about 80x19 or 230x12, in a list of names. Too small to read, so the colour marks tease the work and invite a hover that opens it up. An index with a pulse, for schools and portfolios.

Two or three recent posts as cards, then every other post as one-line rows: date and category 13px, title 14-15px, author right, 36-64px rows on hairlines. No excerpts in the ledger. A long archive stays scannable, and nothing needs pagination.

A newspaper front page: three columns of about 308/632/308px, a large lead tile and 32px title in the centre, stacks of 21px stories in the sides split by 1px rules with four-line clamps. Use only when you have at least five real stories at once.

One post runs full width as a split: 600px art left in a 10px frame, 20-30px title, excerpt and byline right. Below it filters, then a three-column grid of 16:10 thumbnails at radius 12. Needs a real art direction, since the lead image carries the page.

The whole index as a table: 36-42px rows on one line, or 81px rows with a 12px category and date line above a 14px title, author and read time right-aligned, 1px rule between. Filter tabs and search above. Add a 3 percent hover fill.

Rows at magazine scale: 212x285 portrait left, 50/60 serif title, category right-aligned to the top, 2px rules, about 367px pitch. Or a 38px headline and 540px cover with a date column. Type dominates the image, and each story gets a whole viewport's attention.

Text-only cells in a three-column grid: 13px date and category, 24/32 title, avatars and authors pinned to the base, about 240px tall. Separate with space alone and a 3 percent hover fill, or small outlined boxes, radius 0-10. No image means no stock photo problem.

The default: three columns of image-top cards, 8-16px radius, 12px meta, 16-20px title, short excerpt, 24px gaps. Fine for a resource library. It only works with a consistent image treatment, and pin dates to the base so they align across uneven text.

Left 120px rail of categories at 14px, active in bold, beside a two-column grid of cards with a pastel illustration tile, 22/700 title, 14px excerpt and byline. Calm for large archives. Works best with one illustrator, or one rule for every tile.

No card chrome at all. Three or four columns: image, then 20/500 title, one sentence ending in a link, 20-32px gaps, square corners or a shared small radius. Heights may vary. Sits between hairlines on a homepage as a small update section, not an index.

Homepage news as a rail: covers 350x197 at 8px gap starting on the page margin and bleeding past the right edge, title and date beneath, 32px square arrows above right, 'All news' beside them. Set on a tinted or dark band if the page needs a beat.

Active tile 818x460, then strips narrowing to about 188, 90, 42 and 8px, all the same height, radius 6, gap 16. Next stories compress at the edge, so depth is shown in one row. 40px arrow tiles top right, a white 40px title on the art. Stack on phones.

News as a bento: 8px gaps, tone cells with 16px radius and nested 12px images, varied spans, partner lockups on solid brand fills, each image carrying a 26px tinted chip with a mono category. Needs real logos and art. Kinds of tile must differ, not only sizes.

No stock photos: every post gets a cover from one system. Dotted field with a logo plate, line sketch with one accent, lettered cartoon or typographic poster. One rule, one palette, generated per post. It turns a feed into a publication, and is the cheapest way to look art-directed.

Filters as small text tabs, 13px, active a 28px filled pill or raised tone, search or RSS far right, directly under the title. Pagination is plain numerals with the current page a 32px pill. No dropdowns, no count badges, no boxed bar.

A dense dated feed: date divider bars, bracketed categories, handle and time in 8-11px, 14/21 bold titles, 12/18 copy, in up to four ruled columns. Reads as a live wire or a noticeboard. Only for communities and schools that truly post every day.

Two tracks: dates in a left rail of about 328px on a faint 1px vertical line with dots, entries in one 624-720px column, right third empty. No cards. About 110px of space and a 32px title mark a major release, 24px a minor one. Body 16/26, Copy link on each.

Three columns: 14px date, a 1px vertical rail with a 5px dot, a 763px entry column. Date and dot stick about 105px from the top while the entry scrolls, then hand over to the next. Entries may open with a wide art panel. The rail makes time physical.

A sticky rail of years and months beside the feed: 24/500 year with chevron, 15px months, active month ink with a 3px bar. Main column: 14px date, 44/700 title, version pill, lede, two-column sections, then a Shipped by row of 32px avatars. For long histories.

Each release is a ruled row: date in 12px mono caps, 32/400 title and tag chips in a left column of about 400px, screenshot and body in the right column. About 120px padding, hairline between. Reads as a catalogue of real product, so the screenshots must be real.

Dense and factual: 12px date column, version or title 18/500, then rows labelled New, Changed or Fixed in a 12px left column, 14px text, platform subheads in bold. Filter chips on top. For tools whose users read release notes to decide whether to upgrade.

Four latest updates on a shared horizontal rail across the content width: 8-12px dots at about 336px pitch, newest coloured, rest grey. Under each: 15/500 title, 14/20 copy clamped with an ellipsis, 13px mono date. 'View all' below. Compact proof that the team ships.

Each release is a card in a two-column grid: a 16:9 tint with one icon and a thin motif, or a cropped UI on a tint, then 12px date and a 14/500 title that lists items with commas. Scan by colour. Use one tint family, with at most five hues.

Per-day headings 14-16/600 over a 1px rule, a muted line when nothing happened, incident title in a warning colour, then updates with a bold status lead word and 12px timestamp. Plain, complete and honest. Trust comes from showing the empty days too.

A personal or project history: name with a small arrow, date range right-aligned on the same baseline, 13px role beneath, a paragraph, about 60px between entries, no dividers. Or live commit rows joined by a 2px line, the oldest fading to 30 percent.
