Hours as body text, not fine print: 18-20/36, day in a fixed 160px column, time left-aligned in the next, no rules between rows, 1px rules between sections. Then address, a linked phone number, two outline map buttons, a map or photo at 50 percent. Say holiday hours and last entry.

A solid brand card with a title and seven day rows, 15px bold days on 36px rows, 7-on-4 dashed leaders running to the time, beside a real map tile of equal height and radius. Group equal days and show split shifts on two lines. The card is the page's one loud object.

Only what matters today, along the foot of the hero: bold 12px OPEN TODAY over the hours, the address, one action arrow, split by 1px slanted rules. Computed from a schedule, in the visitor's frame. The full table lives on the visit page.

Three columns of quiet cards: 16/600 name, 14px two-line address, clock icon with hours, then View and Order as a pair of 40px buttons pinned low. Group by state with a count and a jump select. Handle Coming soon and Temporary hours in the same slots.

Each venue gets a story: alternating rows on a tinted panel, 30px name, two paragraphs, a 4:3 interior photo, then icon rows split by hairlines for address, transport, today's hours and phone, then View and Book. For places where the room is the reason to come.

One column per office: a thin 105px live analog clock or a grey local time, city at 32-40/600, role label, address and linked phone at 16px, on a 345px pitch. Wraps to two up on phones. Live time turns a list of addresses into proof of a real team.

A list of places with no map: city name then two lines of address, in even columns about 210px wide, or a loose staggered grid of grey tiles about 265 wide fading in. Or city names at 20px over film. Use when the fact of where you are is enough.

The map is a drawn figure, not an embed: pale land on one tone, radius 32, flat pins, and 1px lines rising to 24px city labels at staggered heights, with 'HQ' as a small outline chip and upcoming sites in grey. Say something a Google embed cannot.

A plain band above the footer: Hours, Address, Contact or Order in three columns, 11px caps heads, 12-14px text, day and time aligned, one small button. Everything a visitor needs without leaving the page. The cheapest thing on this list and the most useful.

Two sites treated as two rooms: full-width split panels in two colours with a 42/600 name, a live 'Closed now' status at top right, an aerial photo and a shared map whose pins switch the panel. Or each venue a bold title and times, with its own map alternating sides.

Today's real conditions as data: a small block with live weather and a garden camera link beside a list of booking actions, or a rail of locations each showing hours and live capacity as a bold percentage. Only with a live source.

A full plan-your-visit page: a sticky 11-14px sub-nav of Hours, Directions, Admission, Accessibility, then each as a section with a map tile at 40 percent, a price table, transport tiles and underlined links. Long, plain and complete. Every question answered in text.

Item name left, price right on the same line, description beneath. 16px caps or medium name, 19px or 14px description, about 80px per item, one or two columns, section head large with a heavy 8px rule or 1px rule. No leaders needed if the column stays under 680px.

Price runs inline after the name, as in print: 13px tracked caps name and price in one line, then a 16/24 serif description, 24px between items, 1px hairline between sections, centred featured dishes framed by rows of small diamonds. Two columns on a tinted paper ground.

One centred column about 420-700px on warm paper: 16px tracked caps name, 17px italic ingredients beneath, price inline or on its own line, script or caps section heads, a small OR between choices. Reads as the printed card on the table. For fine dining and prix fixe.

Full-bleed food photo bands of about 360px between courses, and a white 720px card with a soft shadow overlapping each band's foot. Inside, 13px caps course title, then centred run-in lines: bold name, ingredients, price. Text stays on one page while appetite does the selling.

Three columns of identical overhead plates, square, radius 20, gap 24. Name 24px caps, 18px ingredients, one allergen line, 'Order now' or macro columns. Consistent photography is the whole design: same angle, plate and light, so the eye compares food.

A menu landing page: a three-column grid of about 76px framed buttons, one per menu, in the place's own ornament, 20-22px condensed caps, stacking to one column on phones. Use when there are six or more menus, and link each to a real page, not a PDF.

For salons, clinics and trades: tinted panels at radius 24 in two columns, each a category with a 30px title, 16px service rows with right-aligned tabular prices on a 34px pitch, 13px notes under a row, a condition such as a patch test at the foot. A double frame adds care.

A catalogue as text: all items as a list of 14-56px names, some with a year in brackets, the current item's caption beneath, one image at a time beside it. Or huge condensed service names on a 54px pitch with arrows pinned far right. Reads as an inventory.

Each product gets a whole viewport: full-bleed colour or illustrated scene, about 620px art, a 72px title, a 12px caps two-liner, one button, an index badge and a small pager. For ranges of four to eight with real character. Always show a plain list view as well.

Two to four tabs above a shelf of packshots: 48px serif tabs with a dot, or 58px pills, one outlined box at radius 30 clipping a marquee of products. Tabs change the set in place, so a small range feels navigable. One action below.

A catalogue of many: stacked horizontal rails, 22/500 title with a 32px arrow beside it, seven cards at about 194px pitch, prev and next far right, about 24px between rows. Phone shows about 2.1 cards, so overflow is obvious. Consistent thumbnails carry it.

A programme as a list: about 115px rows on 1px rules, a 36px display title left, dates right in grey, no cards. Or a row with image, ticket type, price and a Buy button. For venues and events, the date is the design: sort by it and group past from future.

No card. Two columns on the page grid, 32/40 quote at weight 500, tracking -2%, opening mark hung left of the text edge so the text stays on the grid. Name and role pinned to the base at 14px, customer logo right-aligned on that line. Pair one long quote with one four-word quote.

One quote as a full-width moment: 48 to 64px on 1.05 leading, tracking -2 to -3%, often the page's only serif, 700 to 1220px wide. Mark in the left rail or none. Attribution 14 to 18px below, with square portrait and logo split by a rule. Sits between hairlines or on a quiet field.

A short centred quote between feature blocks, no card: 20 to 28px, 580 to 820px wide, 36 to 48px avatar, 14px name and role, optional logo after a 1px divider. Emphasis by ink: first sentence full ink and the rest muted, or one phrase at weight 500. Stays below headings in weight.

A quote that carries its own numbers. Quote 20 to 60px, then under a hairline two or three figures at 24 to 48px with 12 to 15px labels, or one mono proof point right-aligned. 40 to 64px avatar, logo and story link. Figures must come from the quoted customer.

Two to four cards or a rail, radius 6 to 32, padding 24 to 40, gap 16 to 24. Customer logo top left as the headline, 16 to 20px quote, then 36 to 48px avatar, 14px name and grey role pinned to the base with margin-top:auto. Make one card much shorter than the others.

Text cards where the person is the hook: radius 0 to 24, padding 24 to 40, 15 to 26px quote at the top, two or three line attribution pinned to the base, empty space between. No logo needed. For health, name the theme instead of the person. Hang the opening mark.

Three to five customer logos as tabs above one story. Each tab is a 2px grey rule over a grey logo; the active logo takes brand colour and its rule fills as a 6 to 8s timer. Below: 24 to 36px quote, divider, one big figure or portrait. Pause on hover, stop under reduced motion.

Two columns: 520 to 680px media beside a 28 to 40px quote with hung mark. Media is a candid photo, a duotone portrait, or a grainy plate in the customer's colour with a centred white logo. Avatar and name low; 40px arrows and a story link aligned to the media's base.

One or two panels of loud colour on a quiet page: radius 8 to 40, 400 to 800px tall, 24 to 36px quote with tight leading top left, name and logo pinned low. Unequal widths such as 880 and 432 beat equal ones. Text in a dark tint of the fill. Use once.

Three to five columns 250 to 440px, gap 16 to 22, heights set by real content. Cards radius 8 to 20, 1px pale border, padding 24 to 32, 36 to 48px avatar, 14/600 name, 13px handle or source, 15 to 17px text. Mask the bottom into a 36px Show more pill. Vary lengths threefold.

Two rows of 320 to 350px cards offset half a card, drifting at different speeds, edges masked over 90px. Radius 16 to 30, 1px border, 40px logo tile, 14px name, 14 to 20px quote. One key sentence bold on a highlighter using box-decoration-break:clone. Pause on hover, static under reduced motion.

Cards 320 to 1060px bleed off the right edge, the next one visibly cut as the scroll cue, gap 16 to 24. Heading or rating block fixed at left or above, 36 to 44px arrows or a progress line, scroll-snap on. Best with few substantial quotes. Never autoplay.

The photo is the card. 276 to 690px wide, radius 8 to 32: a portrait with a darkened lower half and 16 to 28px white quote over it, or a photo flush on top with the quote in a tinted body below. The photo must show the real person or the real job.

Masonry of unequal tiles, radius 12 to 32, gap 16 to 32. Portraits with scrim quotes alternate with cream tiles holding award marks and press mastheads, or a tall product photo sits between review columns. Four columns of 288px or two of 495px. The kinds of proof vary, the tile recipe does not.

People talking. Three 375px portrait cards, radius 4 to 20, 22px outcome sentence over a bottom gradient, 64px play ring. Or a wall of 217px talking heads at 4 to 8px gaps beside a 72px count, a name pill on each clip. Captions on, sound off by default.

Third parties, not customers. Score or quote first, outlet as the mark: 332 by 294 outlined cards with a 35px score top left, white publisher logo top right, 19px quote low. Or 14px one-liners under grey mastheads. Keep each outlet's letterforms and link to the article.

Reviews as a public record. Rating row above with score, stars, count and See all, then three columns: star row, 16 to 22px title, 14 to 16px text, tracked name, italic date, no cards or one tint. Keep dates and one mixed review. Best for stores and local services.

Quotes set straight on the page in two to six columns, no cards, only 1px rules at most. 16 to 20px text, justified serif or ragged sans, dash attribution in 15/500 sans, or ruled cells at 40px padding. About 100px of air under a small label and a heavy rule.

The quote takes the shape of speech: a 640px white bubble, radius 28, small tail pointing at a 44px portrait. Or scattered capsules, radius 60, 20px text, two small circles trailing to a round avatar on a soft glow. Short informal lines only, off-grid on purpose.

One person at length. A 766px square paper card with 48px avatar, ruled heading, 16/28 candid bullets and a signature. Or a full-screen question and answer split by 1px rules, one exchange per viewport. Use when you have a real voice and no logos.

Rules above and below. Left column: 14px bold label and one small drawing in the accent colour. Right: 28px regular quote in a five-column measure, then a link. One witty mark replaces avatars, stars and logos.

Testimonials as a client list. Full-width 108px rows on 1px rules: 15px caps project left, 60px radius-8 greyscale portrait with caps name and grey title centred, 56px pale disc with accent plus right. Hover tints the row and blackens the disc; opening reveals the quote.

A review shares a row with something the reader can do: two 546 by 600 cards, 8px gap, radius 24, one a 44px question with 54px pill answers, the other stars, 44/48 quote and a member chip. Proof sits one tap from the decision. Keep legal disclosures visible.

One drifting row of marks flattened to one mid grey, 24 to 32px tall, 56 to 100px gaps, in a 960 to 1320px window with 10 to 12% mask fades at both ends. 12 to 15px caption above or none. 40 to 60s loop, pause on hover, static under reduced motion.

Two rows drifting opposite ways, offset half a logo, in a 190 to 300px band. Raw black or full-colour marks 24 to 60px tall, or cells with 1px rules and a 36px caption strip carrying the count between the rows. Use when the list is long and heavy.

Static row or 6 by 2 grid, marks flattened to one grey near 45 to 60% ink, about 24px optical height, 170 to 196px column pitch, 58 to 107px row pitch, no boxes. 13 to 15px muted caption or none. Deliberately quiet so neighbours keep the attention.

Marks in solid ink or pure white, 24 to 32px tall, no greying: six justified along the hero's base, 6 by 2 at 170px pitch, or a tight 4 by 2 cluster 575px wide in a void. No caption. Confidence comes from strength and the space around.

Marks keep brand colour, 22 to 40px tall, each centred in a drawn page column or between two hairlines: a 72px band under the hero, or 4 by 2 at 100px row pitch. No caption, no boxes. Logo colour is the section's only decoration.

Logos in cells of a shared 1px table, no gaps: 5 by 4 at 275 by 129, or one 66px strip of six cells with a 14px label in the first. Mono marks 24 to 28px tall, centred. A serif phrase may replace the caption. Hover draws a 2px accent bottom edge.

A ruled wall that navigates. Five or six columns, cells 97 to 129px tall, logos at full ink, a small corner arrow on about half the cells, marking those with a written story. Hover tints the cell. A last tile may hold a portrait and one figure.

Each mark in a filled tile: 172 to 291px wide, 64 to 124px tall, gaps 2 to 16, radius 0 to 12, one tone off the page, black mono logos. Tiles give weak logos equal presence. Scatter two accent tints, or run as a marquee at 8px gaps with edge fades.

A grey wall or marquee at 35% ink with exactly one mark in full colour or white, changing on a timer or lit as it passes centre. The small movement proves someone cared. 5 by 6 at 222 by 104, or a 40px masked row.

Marks that do something. Grey wordmarks at 40% with one at full strength and a 2px underline filling as a story timer; or insurers as choices under a price line; or client names in 32px pills that open the work.

No band. Five 20 to 24px grey marks in the text column under the sentence they support, at 86px centres; or a 94px strip on the hero's foot; or a 450 by 56 dock; or marks passing behind the headline. Proof attaches to a claim.

Three to five marks, large and alone: 230px pitch inside a 420px radius-32 panel, 150px press marks on a black band, or black 40px wordmarks on a flat 217px colour band cut by the viewport. A few logos in a lot of room outrank a long strip.

Publications in their own letterforms, one ink, 28 to 34px tall, about 100px gaps or small diamonds between, 12 to 16px AS SEEN IN label. On paper bands the ink takes the page's tone. If it drifts add a visible pause control. Only real coverage.

Recognition as objects: 56 to 120px medals or laurels in two centred rows at 80px pitch, or 70px marks with 16px captions, no boxes. Third-party colour stays, or redraw as grey wreaths with award and year inside. A 52px ledger works for portfolios.

Trust as plain facts: three 106px hairline seals with the label over a faint engraved icon, five 103px ruled cells with 32px line icons above the footer, or 36px chips stating status in words, such as expected Q1 2027. Redraw as one family; never paste vendor badges.

Client names as type, no logos. Three rows of 51px serif at 120px height on 1px rules, 18px hollow circles between, rows sliding opposite ways. Or an alphabetical 14px list in one 480px column, where a gallery and a global brand weigh the same.

Customers shown as your product's own object: a row of 40px app icons with soft shadows, or 240 by 56 org cards with 32px logo, name, plan pill and truncated stats. Reuse the real component. Colour stays because each item is a thing.

Cell size encodes tier: 3-up at 180px, then 5-up at 88px, 12px mono tier label per row, shared 1px rules, marks at 70% ink. Leave unfilled cells empty and end with a faint Become a sponsor cell. Honest for open source and events.

Logos with a number attached: a ruled 120px row with a fixed cell holding a score out of 5 beside a drifting logo cell, or grey marks each above tan stars with a 12px underlined disclosure. Name the source and the date.

The list gets one small idea: a two-column Colourful and Sleek table with a swap button, a drawn beam landing on each logo in turn, or black marks on a painted panel. Only when the brand already jokes. Logos stay fully legible.

Three or four left-aligned columns on the page grid, no cards or rules. Numeral 32 to 56px at 400 to 600, tracking -3 to -6%, tabular figures, 12px gap, 14 to 16px label. About 200px of clear space above. Accent colour only if numerals are few.

Three or four columns under 1px rules: each column its own top rule with 16 to 48px gaps, or one pair of full-width hairlines around the row with 120px padding. Numerals 47 to 96px at 300 to 600, 16px two-line caption. A short accent segment can ride the hairline to mark focus.

Three to five cells sharing 1px rules, rail to rail, about 180px tall, 40px top padding, 16px side padding. Numerals 48 to 64px with -4% tracking at a weight that survives your face, 16px caption, optional mono index or dagger footnote. Stacks unchanged on phones.

Stats as stacked rows. Right 600px column beside a 40px two-tone heading, rows 160px tall on 1px hairlines: 64/400 figure left, right-aligned 16px label over a 12px mono caps note. Or alternate figure, customer logo and one sentence on a dark band.

Each number names whose it is. Three 275px columns under a 1px rule: logo, 42px numeral, 15px descriptor, grey Read the story. Or rows of 24px logo, bold figure and grey rest of phrase at 56px pitch. Or tiles in each customer's colour.

Three or four filled tiles, radius 0 to 12, gap 4 to 20, padding 24 to 36: numeral 44 to 64px, a 20px subject, a 13px explanation. One tone off the page, or near-black on light. Set the disclosure under the row, in plain 13px text.

Cards stepped so the ground shows through: 416 by 162 at radius 32 with the second column 64px lower, or outlined radius-2 cards descending left to right with mono numerals and a live counter. Place beside a photo or falling art, not in a row.

Full-bleed flat band in a deep brand colour, 32px heading, three or four 48 to 96px white numerals, 14 to 24px tinted captions, 64 to 120px padding, no cards. Superscript units at half size. Use once, as the page's one flood.

The figure is drawn, not stated: widths in true ratio (170 beside 988px for 45 and 220 wpm), bars proportional on the page grid, a dot matrix spelling the count, circles counted and crossed, or one hairline curve under 2px-ticked metrics. The scale must be honest.

Reproducible comparison. 3 by 2 cards, 1px rule, 16px gap, 20px padding: 16px title, 13px scenario, four mono race rows with bars and yours in bold, a rule, then accent multiplier and memory figure. Method note and reproduce link below. Bars to scale.

Numbers read as sentences. Centred 64/600 lines at 88px pitch: figure, an inline object at cap height replacing the word space, noun. Or 24px facts split by a rule, or bold figures opening ordinary lines beside a phone. No labels, no cards.

One figure owns the section: 96 to 200px, tight, alone in a band or outlined card, 13 to 14px caption. It may roll on entry or change with scroll. Choose the one number that would surprise someone, and never rest on zero.

White numerals 40 to 130px directly on a photo, 12 to 14px tracked label, darkening only where they sit. Inset the pane 100px or use the photo's dark area. Or small white chips at radius 10 on a close-up. The photo must relate to the number.

A number that is visibly running: tabular 36 to 56px digits, comma-grouped, ticking or rolling, 12px label, small map or filter beside it. State the source and when it last reset. Needs a real feed; otherwise use a dated static figure.

A thin band of facts, not figures: 80px tall, flat tint or graph paper, three 24px/500 statements each led by a 24 to 32px glyph, split by 32px rules. Or 64px custom line icons with 21px labels. Mix numbers and words. Suits stores and local firms.

Scores from named platforms: three units 40px apart with a 32px numeral, five 14px stars and a 13px source. Or tiles, or wreaths around press logos on a quiet 248px band with a 12px disclosure. Real sources only.

Stats that get no section: inside the hero or CTA row, 16 to 24px value over a 14px muted label, about 40px apart or split by 1px rules 58px tall. Or 32px pills under the subhead. Baseline-matched to the button.

Wide quote cells alternate with narrow metric cells: 1px border, one corner colour wash, 30px display text, mono caps label, logo at base. Or one card of stacked figures beside a 2 by 2 analyst grid on a darker ground.

A table of customers. Rows 56 to 120px, on a 1px rule or none at 96px pitch: 14px name, one-line result, grey logo, 11px mono caps tag, right-aligned READ STORY. Hover fills the row, inset 8px from the page. Finish with a Your company row.

Three or four columns, no borders: a 4:3 or 16:10 tile in a pale tone, flat brand colour or greyscale still with a large centred logo, then 14 to 18px title and a mono tag or Read story link below the tile. Gutters 16 to 24, radius 4.

Three 400 by 480 tiles or a rail of 332 by 430, radius 0 to 6, each with custom art in that customer's palette, big centred logo, small wordmark bottom left. Below: 16/22 two-line result and accent link. Art must be art; a bare gradient reads as missing.

Four 80px logo cells as tabs, active cell shaded. Below, 50/50: left bottom-aligned caps label and a 32px two-tone metric headline, right a photo bleeding to the rails. Or half stat, half photo. One customer on screen at a time.

One open, the rest collapsed: a 752 by 340 gradient card beside 76px logo strips, or an open row with halftone photo and white stat pills over 80px closed rows with 48px logo tile and 24px headline. Transition width over 400ms.

One card, radius 12, 1392 by 470, split 60/40. Left a full-bleed still quiet enough for a co-brand lockup, 56px play disc, mono WATCH label. Right white: logo, 34 to 36px tight quote, 16px name, 12px mono role, two buttons pinned low.

Mixed cells at 2 to 16px gaps, radius 0 to 24. White cells on a deep ground: 64px stat over a rule, caption, logo foot, beside a wide quote cell with inset portrait and stacked name tags. Or a neon quote block beside a logo tile. Two cell recipes at most.

One image edge to edge, 740px or viewport tall, no radius, breaking the page margins. White caption bottom left at 32px inset: 15/500 name over 15px mono type. No scrim. Or fade the bottom third into the page and set logo and statement on the fade.

Darkened customer photo tiles, 310 to 575px, radius 0 to 12, tinted 30 to 40%, large white logo, 24px result line, small glass button. Or black 360 by 460 cards where a photo fades in on hover behind the same logo.

One story per page with controls you can count: a 416px copy column beside an 848 by 477 image, mono 01 / 05 between 28px arrows, copy crossfading. Or a centre slide 578px wide with cropped neighbours. Never autoplay without a pause.

Result first, no photo: 404 by 372 white cards, radius 16, 8px gap, bleeding both edges on a grey ground, 56px grey logo tile, 24/39 outcome line, 14px client at base, heading below the rail. Or a screenshot in a cream well above tags.

Agency index. Two to four columns, 12 to 16px gutters, media-led, radius 0 to 24, mixed aspect ratios so rows interlock, 12 to 14px title and grey tag beneath, no card chrome. Filter pills 24 to 32px above, active filled.

The story as text. A sticky label column (Challenge, Solution, Products) at 13 to 15px beside a product fragment on a tint, or three ruled columns with the finding in bold and a link to the source. Substance replaces imagery.

The customer's real product in a scene: a 418px live site floating on a 558px photo card, a dark app window cropped in a 720px colour block that checkers with the next case, or a bordered browser card beside a plain heading.
Three or four 1px cards, radius 0, 204px video with 56px play disc and name on a scrim, mono company, 20px headline stating one fact, 14px copy, CTA pinned low. Talks from real events work best.

Four to six columns of greyscale portraits, 4:5 or square, radius 0 to 4, gutters 8 to 68. Name 13 to 15px at 400 or 500, role 11 to 14px grey. Same head size and light across the set. Group by office under 32px titles.

Different people cut onto one ground: 170 to 320px portraits, radius 0 to 24, a single warm or neutral backdrop, 14 to 18px name, muted credentials. Separate headshots read as one shoot, even when taken years apart.
Each person on a flat colour: pastels in 5-column white cards, saturated tiles with a white name strip, or a gradient strip with no gaps. Pick from three or four fills. Cut-outs need clean edges.

A tall tile as the card: 370px dark tile, radius 20 to 32, cut-out rising from the base, translucent 56px label inset 8px with 18px name and 15px role. Or a photo above two 42px pills for role and LinkedIn.

People as qualifications. 300 by 170 gradient cards with cut-out doctor, title and specialties on a 2px rule, or a 282 by 353 rail with a verified mark. Name 16 to 18px with degrees, role and institution stated. Short bio below the card.

Many people, small. Three columns at 408px pitch, rows 153px: 96px square portrait radius 8, 18px name, 14px grey role, 20px social glyphs and a flag. Or gutter ticks with name, affiliation and pill. End with a Could be you tile.
Everyone else as text: four columns at 336px pitch, 16px grey names on 39px lines under the portraits, no photos. Or 13px associates, or mono label and value rows. Scales to hundreds without effort.

One named person as the pitch. 50/50: a 676 by 1000 greyscale portrait cropped to the waist beside a bio in the page's display serif at 63/68, link pinned to the photo's base. Or a 56px greeting on ink beside an offset-framed portrait.

Real people in a real place: two 670 by 376 snapshots, 34px gutter, no radius, 13px caps caption naming everyone in frame. Or a staff photo in a 16px frame beside a contact trio. Imperfect light is a feature.

Volume as proof. 100 greyscale 36 to 60px avatars in a perspective wall or rows fading at the edges, one turning full colour with a mono name tag, one line above stating the true count. Real contributors only.

Portraits in one commissioned hand: black-line busts on a 1px rule with skin as the only fill, hatched circles on a dotted bus line, or depth-of-field overlap with the focused face sharp. The treatment is the signature.
Backers, small and quiet: two flat 140px tiles with firm marks and 11px partner names, or a row of 32px portraits with name and firm captions under a 48px Backed by line. Sits after the team.
No team grid at all. Three full-width 48px rows on 1px rules: 14px grey label left, 14/500 link with arrow right. A question, a next step and a jobs link replace faces.

A catalogue. Ruled 1248px grid, 32px padding, mono caps category, logos 26px tall in wrapping rows, last item a grey mono + Any SAML / OIDC. Or three columns of 65px rows: 20px line icon, 14px name, 14px grey descriptor. Brand colour stays.

Your product as the hub. A 96px dark tile centred in a tinted panel at radius 28, 48px white icon tiles stacked 5 left and 6 right, 1.5px grey beziers landing on the hub at slightly different heights. A hairline, then three named one-liners.

Four to six columns of 183 by 124 tiles, gaps 8 to 16, radius 0 to 8, pale fill, 40 to 44px logo over 15/600 label. Final tile is an ellipsis meaning any tool. Text link centred below, pill toggle above if there are modes.

Scannable directory. Three columns of 44px tiles, 1px border, radius 8, 16px gap, 20px colour logo, 15px grey name, last tile View all. Or 40px icon tile and 16px label at 68px pitch, with a 21+ more pill below.

Icons in a row that dissolves. 64 to 96px square tiles, dark or translucent, radius 2 to 20, white or colour glyphs, 128px pitch or two offset rows, masked at the ends so the list feels unending. Copy holds the opposite side.

Tokens on rings: four concentric 1px rings cropped by a 384px card, 48px round logo tokens on them, brand mark centred. Or 72px white discs drifting at varied heights behind a heading, with a 64px search pill as the real action.

Two edge-bleeding rows offset half a card: 260 by 142 white cards, 1px border, radius 8, 48px icon tile, mono tag top right, 11px mono type label, 20px name. Hovered card tints. Shows a catalogue with real contents.

36px pills, soft fill, 16px glyph, 15/500 label, 8px gaps, wrapping under the subhead. Unavailable items sit at 50% opacity, so the row also states status. Or centred white pills fading at the last row to imply more.

Marks only, one ink: seven 48px solid framework marks on a 124px pitch beside copy, or a 6 by 3 grid of 40px grey connector logos in the right half. No tiles, no labels. Works when the audience already knows the marks.
A real repository as proof: a 57px row between hairlines with GitHub mark, 16/500 repo name, then language dot, star icon, count and arrow in 14px grey. Styled as table data, fetched live.

Card with no fill or shadow on a slightly tinted page: 1px line at 8-10% ink, radius 2-8, padding 32, 20/500 title, 16/24 muted copy, then one real object pinned to the base, such as a command field, sketch or logo, the only white thing in the row.

Text-only outline card: 1px line, radius 4-16, 16-28 padding, 12px mono or caps label, 16-20px title, one short muted line, no icon tile, no shadow. Keep it compact at about 160px tall. Hover darkens the border, not the fill. Suits docs indexes and capability lists.

Horizontal pointer card, full column width, 70-114px tall: 8px padding, 1px line, radius 12-16, 64-96px thumbnail at outer radius minus padding, 16px title, 14px accent action, 32px round arrow chip pinned bottom right, 16px gap between rows. Hover darkens only the border.

The card works as a picture mat: page one tone off card, radius 16, padding 8 all round, image radius 8-10 so corners nest, then 16-24px text inset. Byline row carries a 1px hairline leader between author and read time. Good for blogs and case studies with strong images.

Two nested layers: outer white card radius 16-24 with 1px line, inner tinted well inset 8px at outer radius minus 8, holding seals, a tick list or live component. Title row sits in the shell, proof sits in the well. Well gives a place for evidence without a second border weight.

No border, no shadow, one tone step off the page, about 2-5% lightness. Radius 8-32, padding 32-56. Title 20-32px light or medium, muted copy, one link. Depth comes from tone alone, so it stays calm at any size. Use warm greys on white, and steps of 6-10 on dark.

Card with copy top-left and a real interface fragment that starts about 48px in and runs past the right and bottom edges, rounded only at its one visible corner. Card clips it. Fragment must stay dense to the crop. Radius 12-32, 24-32 padding, 24px title. Never pad the fragment on all sides.

Pure image tile, radius 20-28, no border or shadow, phone or crop clipped by the tile. Caption sits outside on the page ground, inset about 15px from the tile edge, bold lead-in then muted sentence. Tiles run as a carousel with circular arrows. The picture stays uninterrupted.

Full-bleed photo tile, radius 0-12, 12-24px gaps, scrim only where text sits: a bottom gradient to 50-60% black or a side wash. 20-34px white title 24-40px in, round arrow bottom right. Better still, take the scrim colour from the image so the field looks native.

Image or colour band on top about 40-60% of height, tinted body below in a colour taken from the brand or image, radius 12-24, 20px gaps. 24px title, 16/27 copy, hairline and small mono label over the image. Row can bleed off the edge with the next card peeking.

Warm off-white tile with fine SVG noise at 30-45% multiply, radius 16-24, 1px ink line at 5%. Name top-left, price or prompt bottom-left, deliberately empty middle. One tile in a row may swap paper for a grainy colour mesh to mark the pick. Reads as a physical sample.

Card whose subject is a number. Plans: 20/500 name, 40/600 price, 12px tag, 13px note, ticks at 30px pitch, 36px full-width button. Proof: mono label, 48px figure, 18px caption low, faint texture in one corner. Numbers use tabular figures and align across the row.

Flat saturated or pastel cards, no border or shadow, radius 0-35, 16-48px gaps. Each card owns one fill and text is set in a dark tint of that fill rather than black. Three at most in a row, on a neutral or black ground. Use where the brand is colour-led.

Ordinary card with one owned edge: a chamfer cut across about 100-167px, a white circle biting a corner to hold a 46px arrow, a folded 32px corner, or a 3-8px coded top bar. Repeat the same edge on every card and clip so it becomes the site's shape.

White card, no visible border, radius 8-18, on a tinted ground, 24-56px padding, one soft tinted shadow around 0 6px 12px -2px at 15-25%. The default most sites overuse. Keep it for objects that really float or for a single featured card, and vary the height of one card to break the row.

Large section panel one tone off the page, radius 12-28, no border or shadow, 34-120px padding. Either one centred statement, or left copy with product UI bleeding off an edge. One grey carries the whole page, so warm it slightly. Usually 1024-1392px wide, inset 24px from the viewport.

One panel in the inverse of the page: white on near-black, or a deep colour on white. About 1020-1392px wide, radius 8-28, 24px from viewport edges, 460-630px tall, generous empty field around a 40-64px statement or a diagram. It becomes the brightest object on the page, so use once or twice.

Full-width brand colour slab with 12-36px margins and a large radius of 24-69px, breaking a white rhythm: 36-60px white heading left, UI or a white list card right. One per page. Radius this large needs a width over 1000px or it looks like a pill.

Sections are physical sheets: a next section with 24-40px top corners slides over the last, or rooms of colour with 32px radius are separated by 40px of page. Inner cards step down to 24px. Use a section colour drawn from that section's image. Works on phones unchanged.

The page sits inside a frame: a white or paper sheet inset 16-36px from the viewport over a brand colour or white desk, top radius 0-16, or a dark image window inset 16px with up to 120px top corners and a 2-3px pale rim. Colour survives as a thin gutter.

Dark shell radius 16 with 4px padding around panes radius 12, so panes share a gutter instead of borders. 44px title row with logo left and 12px muted context right. Inner radius always equals outer minus gap. Sits on a grainy plate with a 0 16px 40px -12px black shadow.

Single bordered panel, 1280 wide, 1px line, radius 8-16, split into 2-3 cells by shared single rules, no gaps. 40px padding: 16px title, 14px copy, link, then a visual filling the rest, and an optional centred pill at the foot. One object, several ideas.

Large neutral panel, radius 16-40, 1344-1400px wide, 20px gutter, 406-580px tall, with an oversized product render cropped by the panel and a white info card overlapping it at the same radius. Or a photo dissolving by gradient into a flat colour drawn from itself, with copy on the fade.

Panel outline carries the idea: white blocks notched into hero art on 12px gaps, a stepped or chamfered corner, a ~400px dome. Cut corners stay rounded by 4-12px at each join. Keep every other surface plain, and repeat the same cut on one more object so it reads as language.

Section presented as an app window: radius 12-20, soft 40px shadow, only two 14px hairline controls top right and no fake traffic lights, internal scroll, 8px inset from a 40px global bar. Enough chrome to sell the idea. Suits playful devtools; never for a serious finance page.

A small fixed object that hugs its content: 56px caption tray, 160px note, or 384px news card, 16-24px from viewport edges, radius 3-16, hairline plus soft 0 4px 24px shadow, close control included. It reads as a physical note, not a chat bubble. One per page, dismissible.

No fill or border: a statement framed only by four 1px L-brackets, 40px each arm, in the accent colour across about 1360x350. Centre 30/38 text at about 85% ink. The brackets do the work of a card while the page stays open. Works best on dark or technical pages.

Full-bleed band split 50/50 into two tints of one hue, 0 radius, flat. UI cards and devices straddle the seam and overlap the section above. Or columns of one template repeated in different hues. Colour does the layout, so keep type simple and shadows off.

A self-contained module inside a magazine grid, radius 0-8, 300px wide: caps title, thumbnail, status line and a full-width action in one accent colour, closed by a 4px rule. It behaves like a boxed feature in print, so it needs a dense surrounding grid to look at home.

Unloaded images hold their true aspect in flat ~#e9e9e9 blocks, no shimmer or icon, then fade in over 300ms. The layout never shifts during scroll. Quiet, and much more expensive-looking than a skeleton pulse. Give every image an explicit aspect-ratio.

Borderless tiles one tone off the page, radius 20-40, 16-24 gaps, no shadow. Rows use opposing splits such as 60/40 then 33/67. 24px title inset 32-40px with muted second phrase, no paragraph. Each tile holds different evidence: UI, seal, logos, number. Art runs off a corner.

Tiles with 1px line, radius 12-16, 12-24 gaps, on a 12-column grid: 2-up over 3-up, or one tall tile beside two short. White or warm tint, 24-32px inset, 18-24px title, key phrase in full ink and the rest muted. Tile edge crops the product. Optional 36px arrow top right.

Each tile is a shell plus well: 1px hairline shell radius 22, 8px padding, tinted well radius 14-16 holding a small white UI object, centred with air around it. Title and one muted line sit in the shell beneath. Rows alternate 2:1 and 1:2, 16px gaps. Keep the UI small.

One frame split by 1px rules instead of gaps: grid gap 1px on a line-coloured background, cells opaque. Outer radius 0-20, no cell fills, row heights 240 and 360 mixing 400/800 and 400/400/400. UI crops fade into the ground by mask. 18px title with arrow bottom-left.

Tiles of 584 and 280 wide, 418 tall, 24 gaps, radius 20-24, no border. Each tile has one vertical gradient or inner bloom, 30px padding, 20/600 title, 15/24 body, then a product fragment cropped by the bottom or right edge. Gradients come from one family. Rows mirror their spans.

Each tile owns one flat fill from a short family, radius 24-40, 8-50px gaps, widths deliberately unequal. 36-40px heading, one visual per tile, closing bar or arrow. Colour separates, so no borders or shadows. Keep the family tight: four steps of one temperature, not a rainbow.

Photo tiles and solid data tiles share one rhythm: same radius 24-40, same 16-20px gap, same title anchor at bottom-left 32px in. Dark-gradient photos alternate with flat brand fills, and figures sit in the solid tiles. Good for consumer, public and impact pages.

Charcoal tiles #1e1e1e, 20px radius, 1px #2c2c2c border, device and widget crops tilted about 6 degrees and bleeding past the base, one large tile with an accent edge glow. Tilt is the only flourish, so keep the type upright and caps titles at 24px.

Four 284px masonry columns, 16px gap, tinted note cards radius 20, 28px avatar, 14px name, 17/24 text, right-aligned grey counts, with long posts spanning two columns and images on top. Heights come from real content, so it never looks gridded. Good for community and social proof.

Nothing is rounded: images, cells, fields and buttons are all 0, with at most one round element such as a help button. Structure comes from rules, gutters and fill steps. Suits fashion, galleries, investors and editorial. Needs excellent photography and type, because nothing softens the page.

Two tight steps: 2 or 4px on controls and cards, up to 6-8px on large media, nothing higher. The corner is barely visible, yet it stops frames reading as raw rectangles. Feels like instruments and drafting. Good for finance, devtools and infrastructure.

Two radii with two meanings: containers small, 2-20, every interactive control a full pill. Shape alone says what is clickable, without colour. Pair 4 with pill for a sharp feel, 12 with pill for a soft one. Never round a container and square a button.

Inner radius equals outer radius minus the gap between them, at every level: 16/12 with a 4 gap, 25/15 with 10, 42/34 with 8, 30/25 with 5. When the gap reaches half the outer radius, floor at the next step of a fixed scale. Pills stay pills. Nothing sits between steps.

Radius assigned by role, with gaps between tiers: 40 section cards, 16 inner cards, 12 chips, 9999 buttons. Or 28 cards, 10 chips, full round on icons. Roughly halve each step with element size. Count how many radii the page uses: three plus pill is enough.

Radius doubles with element size: 16 tiles, 32 cards, 64 media, 128 wide panels, pill buttons, or 69 slabs with 42 wells. Huge panels still feel related to small tiles, and the curve becomes the brand shape. Needs wide elements and a friendly consumer tone.

Tiles are square at 0, and a wrapper clips the whole group at radius 30 with overflow hidden, so four images read as one object. A 4px page-colour gap acts as a thin cross. Inner corners stay sharp. Good for galleries of equal images.

All structure by 1px lines at 7-10% ink, no shadows on page elements, so depth belongs only to product UI inside mock-ups. On pure black tint the line cool, about rgba(214,235,253,.19) on r8. Requires a precise grid: every line is visible, so every misalignment is too.

Two 1px verticals run the full page at the container edges, inverting across dark and light sections. Horizontal rules snap onto them with ~6px hollow square nodes, and overshoot 40-48px past the frame, fading out. Every section reads as cut from one sheet. Strong devtool signature.

Frame implied by corners only: ~12px L ticks 1-3px thick, ~12px outlined squares, or detached 1px rails sitting 16px off the tile and never meeting. Reads as print crop marks. Apply to section containers, never inner cells. Works with a muted tint per section.

Dark card, radius 24, 1px cool line at 15-19%, plus a second 1px line just inside the top edge running the middle 50%, brightest at centre and fading both ways, and a faint radial glow below it. One light source for every card. Hover can slide the highlight.

Highlight the chosen plan with the same card and a 1px accent keyline at 40-50%, a 4px accent halo at 8-10%, and the only filled button in the row. No scale-up, ribbon or fill change. A variant fades the 2px outline from transparent at the top to strongest at the base.

Two lines around one object: a 2px outer line, ~4px paper gap and 1px inner line for a printed menu feel, or a solid 1px inner with a dashed outer offset ~5px to mark a selected object. Or a 1px rectangle offset 14px behind a photo. Use on few, chosen objects.

Line style carries data. Solid hairlines for the core product and 1px dashed cells for the paid tier, or green borders for paths and grey for utilities. Readers learn the code without a legend. Limit to two styles and keep both at the same weight and alpha.

An almost invisible outer rim around a lifted inner panel: outer radius 25, 1px line at 6-10%, 10px padding, inner fill one step up at radius 15. Or a solid 8px pale ring around dark media, outer 42, inner 34. The rim sets the object apart with no shadow.

Panels interlock like puzzle pieces: a stair-step bite of about 65px rise and 220px run from a corner, every join rounded at 12px, and a separate patch fills the bite leaving a 12px page channel. Repeat one angle or step on buttons and tags.

The browser window itself is framed: a fixed 1px rule 22px in with a tiled ground outside, content scrolling inside; or a 10px brand strip across the very top with no header bar. Strong concept. Suits one expressive brand and needs a real reason.

1px rule at about 10% ink, content width and never full bleed, 80px clear above and below, on a single background. Rules do all the section pacing. Use the same line for index rows at a narrower width, and a final full-ink rule to mark the end of content.

Faint 1px rule, 6-10% ink, runs edge to edge between sections with 64px padding either side and no colour bands. The page feels ruled rather than boxed. Suits fashion, galleries and research sites where images supply the interest.

2px solid ink rule across the full content width, about 8px under a 15px label, used as the only divider on the page. Its weight closes a section the way a magazine rule does. A variant runs the first 62% solid and the rest at 20%, like a progress marker.

Two line types with two jobs. Solid 1px for structure, and round 1px dots about 6px apart for rows, breaking at column gutters. Or solid under H2 and dashed under H3. Draw dots with a radial gradient, because CSS dotted spacing cannot be set.

List row with a 1px hairline stretching across free space between title and meta, like a contents page: flex-1 leader, 42px row height, 12-15px text, right-aligned tag and date. The leader carries the eye 800px across. Darken it on hover instead of filling the row.

One 1px vertical at about 6% white runs the feed at the rail's left edge, ~7px dots marking each date. Newest dot in the only colour on the page chrome, older dots dim. Content sits in a separate column about 320px right. Made for changelogs.

Section label as a ~53px strip between two 1px rules: 13px bold label left, 13px muted date right, no large heading. Or a brand stripe of two 8px bars with a 4px gap, used exactly once. Rules and one bold word do the work of a headline.

Sections meet along a shape rather than a line: a straight 6 degree slant, a ~1200px flat ellipse tinted 2%, a ~150px corner tab, or one SVG torn edge. Echo a shape already in the hero. Use once or repeat exactly, and keep it quiet in colour.

Instead of a rule, small marks: two 12px L ticks opening a section, a ~44px band of 1px ticks at uneven 14-27px spacing, or a 30px arrowhead on a grid corner. Barely visible, and they add a measuring-instrument tone. One device only.
A single full-bleed deep colour band interrupts a white shelf to promote one thing: 18px headline left, image bleeding off the bottom right. Used once. Works because everything around it is uniform.

Two layers per level: a hue-tinted layer 0 30px 60px -12px at 25% and a black layer 0 18px 36px -18px at 30%. Blur is twice y, and spread pulls in so nothing leaks past the top. Scale y 2, 6, 13, 30, 50. For a contact-only look set spread to minus y.

Three layers with three jobs: 0 0 0 .5-1px ring at 10-13% draws the edge, 0 1px 1px at 4-7% makes contact, 0 2px 4px at 4% or 0 14px 34px -10px at 18% lifts. Tint the colour with the page's ink. Replaces the border, and stays crisp on any ground.

Solid duplicate with no blur, offset down and right: 3-6px on small items, 12-24px on large panels, 1px outline on the object, 0 radius or a small one. Reserve it for few key objects. Every other surface stays flat, which is what makes this one lift. Has a printed feel.

A huge faint halo: blur about 120px at 3-4%, gone 70px past the edge, plus a tight 0 2px 16px contact, or 0 10px 40px at 6-10% tinted by the ground. It washes into the page and is only just perceptible. Good on one hero object on a pale ground. Multiple blooms turn to fog.

Base frames carry no shadow at all. Only objects in motion or fixed above the page do: a caption tray at 0 4px 24px 10%, a rising clip visible 40px past its edges. A shadow therefore means this layer moves, so the page reads as flat until it matters.

Depth by overlap instead of shadow: a white sheet with 16px top radius slides over the last section while that section dims from #eaeaea to #d1d1d1. Or a section ends in 60px bottom corners with a soft tinted shadow on a pale layer. The page behaves like stacked sheets.

Sheets tilted about 2 degrees with a second sheet offset behind, heading and body rotating with the card so it reads as a physical object. ~24px radius, no blur shadow. Reserve for a single playful moment on a consumer page. Never tilt a card that holds a form.

Sticky bar over scrolling content: blur 12-20px, fill 62-72% of the page colour, 1px line. Blur must be strong enough that large headings passing beneath turn to soft smears, otherwise type collides with the links. This is where nearly all real glass lives.

Same bar shape, two skins. Over light content it is light glass. Over a dark section or footer it flips to translucent near-black with a 1px white 10% ring, white links and a light CTA with a dark label. Detect by scroll position, not blend modes.

No bar background at all. Each nav group gets its own ~16px blur patch with ~40px feathered edges, or the top 76px blurs through a gradient mask, so cards melt out under the logo. Content stays sharp between groups. Build with mask-image on a backdrop-filter layer.

Small caption tray over changing media: rgba(255,255,255,.5) with blur ~20px, radius 3-6, width hugging the text. It turns olive over lime and pale cyan over cyan, so it belongs to each image. Text stays dark with a 58% second line, since blur removes the detail that hurts reading.

Cards over a single close photograph: white at 7-20%, blur, radius ~24, 12px pill tags, hairline, 28px title. The photo tints them, so colour comes from the image. Needs a dark or mid-tone photo and a row that bleeds off the right edge.

Large panel, 1040-1160px, radius 12-28, measured fill only 30% near-white with heavy 30-40px blur and a 1px line, over one object that crosses its edge: a ribbon dissolves beneath it and turns crisp past the border. That crossing is what shows the glass. Over a smooth gradient, nothing shows.

Small frosted card straddling the edge of a photo: 273x198 translucent cream, radius ~12, or a 632px panel overlapping a corner by ~210px at 60% dark. Half on image, half on page, so the blur is visible and the text stays readable. Use once beside large imagery.

Headline in a neo-grotesque or geometric sans, weight 450-600, 48-72px, line-height 1.0-1.1, tracking -0.02 to -0.03em, one near-black or near-white ink, two lines broken by hand at a phrase, 24-44 characters. Sub at 16-20px, one ink step down, 16-32px below.

Headline at 56-108px in a sans of weight 400-600 or a high-contrast serif, tracking -0.045 to -0.07em, line-height 0.95-1.1, under 50 characters. Stop while every letter pair still shows a sliver of ground; faces with a tight display cut stop near -0.045em. Relax as size falls: -0.06em at 64px, -0.04em at 48px, -0.015em at 32px.

Headline at weight 400 only, 48-116px, line-height 1.0-1.1, tracking -0.01 to -0.03em, black or warm near-black, flush left, one line if it fits. Allow no bold heading anywhere on the page. Hierarchy comes from size and ink alone; labels drop to 11-13px mono or small caps.

Headline in a weight 200-300 sans, at least 64px on light and 48px on dark, tracking -0.02 to -0.04em, line-height 0.85-1.1, one or two lines, on a plain ground. Keep controls at weight 500 so the thin type reads as a decision, not a font-loading fallback.

Headline in weight 700 sentence case, 48-80px, line-height 1.0, tracking -0.025 to -0.035em, near-black, a short plain sentence ending in a full stop. H2s keep the ratio at about 42/48 and -0.035em, two lines at most. Never leave tracking at default on bold.

One serif used only for H1 and H2, weight 300-500, 44-80px (up to 128px on dark manifesto pages), line-height 1.0-1.1, tracking 0 to -0.03em, single ink, never bold. All UI, labels and body stay sans or mono, so the serif alone carries the voice.

One serif family, 54-96px, weight 300-500, line-height 0.95-1.1, tracking -0.01 to -0.03em. Turn one word or the closing phrase into the true italic at the same size and weight, usually on line two. The italic must carry the meaning. Sub in full ink at weight 500, not pale grey.

Grotesque heading, weight 450-600, 48-88px, tracking -0.01 to -0.02em. One word or phrase swaps to an italic serif at weight 400 on the same line. Scale the swap to match x-heights, usually 1.02-1.1em, and reset its tracking to 0. One swap per heading, repeated through H2s.

One size, 32-64px, weight 400-600, line-height 1.0-1.25, tracking 0 to -0.03em. Two clauses split by tone: first at full ink, second at 45-60% ink, on a second line or running on. Alternatives: drop weight two steps, or change case. This block replaces the subhead.

Headline in one ink with a single clause or final line in one flat brand colour, no gradient, same size and weight, 46-80px, line-height 1.0-1.1. The coloured words are the claim, not decoration. Repeat the hue on the primary action, or take it from the hero photograph.

Clip a small tonal gradient to the headline: full ink at top-left to 60-70% ink at bottom-right, no hue shift, 52-96px, weight 400-500, on a dark or pale ground. It should read as light falling on letters. Keep the first words at full ink so the line stays crisp.

Flat ink headline, 60-128px, with only the closing phrase clipped to a two-stop gradient taken from the logo or a product colour, or with one dark stop near the ink so the shift is subtle. Never gradient the whole headline. Repeat on H2s only if it is the signature.

One word in a 44-90px headline gets one mark: an SVG hand stroke 3-6px thick under the baseline, a flat highlighter block, or a selection rectangle of radius 4-6px. Overrun the word by 4-10px, break at descenders, and vary the stroke between headings so it never looks stamped.

Uppercase headline in a condensed or neo-grotesque cut, 56-120px, line-height 0.8-0.95, tracking 0 to -0.04em, short lines of near-equal length so the text locks into one block. Pair with thin sentence-case body at 16-20px. Reserve it for headlines, never nav or labels.

Extended black cut, weight 700-900, uppercase or sentence case, 40-78px, line-height 0.8-1.05, tracking 0 to -0.01em, two to four short lines. Width supplies the presence, so size can stay modest. Set everything around it small and light, at 13-18px.

One display face with strong character (soft serif, chunky rounded, fat retro, custom) at weight 400-800, 48-90px, line-height 0.95-1.2, tracking 0 to -0.02em, in a deep brand colour instead of black, on a flat or pastel ground. Keep the sans beside it completely plain.

H1 at only 28-48px, weight 400-500, line-height 1.1-1.3, one or two lines, and nothing on the page is larger. On utility pages use one word at 48-64px with 90-120px of air above and below. Scale comes from images, tables or whitespace, never from the type.

The product or brand name alone is the headline, 56-80px, weight 500-600, tight tracking, centred, no verb. Beneath it a five or six word promise at 21-28px weight 400, roughly 2:1 with the name. A short status word can replace the promise. Let the object fill the frame.

Two short lines at 100-390px, line-height 0.75-1.05, tracking -0.02 to -0.04em, anchored to a corner or stepped across the viewport instead of centred, running past the fold or overlapped by images. No subhead beside it. Use once, on a page of quiet small type.

Each headline line rests on its own 1px rule in the pale line colour, either cut to that line's width for a stepped edge or full-bleed like ledger paper. 72-125px, weight 300-400, rule 8-14px under the baseline. Keep rules very quiet.

Fixed opening words with one slot at the end cycling 3-5 nouns, masked to the line height and moved vertically over 400-600ms, or typed with a cursor. Reserve the widest word's width, or centre so the whole line re-centres. Hold each word 2-3 seconds. Stop for reduced motion.

A full sentence or list takes the headline job, 35-80px, weight 400-500, line-height 1.1-1.2, with no size or weight change inside it, running 60-100% of the container. Break lines by hand. Allow at most one inline object or underlined link. No subhead follows.

One paragraph at 32-48px, weight 300-500, line-height 1.0-1.2, left aligned, 780-1150px wide. First sentence in full ink, the rest runs on in the same line at about 6:1 contrast. No eyebrow, no subhead. Repeat for nearly every section. Use text-wrap: pretty, never balance.

Two lines at 26-34px, weight 350-500, tight tracking: set-up in 50% ink, payoff in solid ink. Reverses the usual order so the eye lands on the last words. Any sub sits 6-8px below. Align the block's bottom edge to the neighbouring image, not its centre.

Left or centred stack repeated identically on every section: label at 12-20px, H2 at 36-52px weight 500-600, lede at 18-21px line-height 1.4-1.55 in the second ink, capped at 640-840px. Gaps 8-24px. Keep the three steps in one family, or two at most.

A short sentence with a full stop and no eyebrow, rule or subhead, 40-64px, weight 400-600, near-black, flush left or centred, 60-120px of air above and 24-64px below. Two short beats work well. It works only if the sentence states something specific.

Split the row: heading 40-88px on the left, a 16-22px note on the right, top or bottom aligned to the heading, starting just right of centre at about 55% of the container, 420-560px wide. A rail-to-rail rule about 60px below may close the row.

Two-line heading at 32-56px on the left; on the same bottom baseline at the far right one small control: a 32-48px button, text link, arrow pair or count. 40-64px down to content. Put the section action here rather than under the grid.

Each section opens with a 1px rule across the container, or 4px for editorial. Heading at 28-60px hangs 12-16px under it in the left third, broken by hand onto two tight lines; content starts on the same line in the next column. Never centre.

Heading sits in a ruled grid cell with a small index: a 16-30px number in muted ink or accent mono beside or above it, matching nav numbering if any. Title 30-80px weight 400, cell padding 24-40px. A folder-style slug can replace the number on developer pages.

Same size throughout, 30-56px: heading opens in sans 600 or serif roman, then turns to an italic serif at weight 400 for the feeling words. Optionally tint the italic one warm accent. Centred or left. Use on every section so it becomes the voice.

Heading in one ink, 36-64px, with one word, clause or line in an accent. The colour must mean something: product family, brand or section hue. On dark, one lit word can take a soft 20-24px glow of its own colour. One coloured element per heading.

One phrase in a 32-64px heading sits on a device: flat highlighter block, selection rectangle of radius 4-6px, bounding box with corner handles, inline code chip, or hand stroke. Choose the device the product itself uses. Same device on every section; the tint may change.

Every section opens with a loud block: 56-110px heavy or condensed caps, line-height 0.85-1.0, plus a quiet contrast voice directly above or below it, such as a 36px italic serif or 20px mono caps. Two tones of voice in one heading unit.

Modest heading in caps at 20-40px, tracking +0.04 to +0.1em, weight 400-600, in ink or a deep brand colour, left or centred. Reads as engraved, not shouted. Pair with a text link on the same baseline. Keep it under 30 characters.

A small line drawing about 85px tall centred above a serif heading at about 56px weight 500, 28px gap, 90px before content. Every major section opens the same way with a different drawing, so drawings act as chapter marks. Needs real illustration, not icons.

The heading is tied to scroll: pinned about 90px below the nav at 48px weight 300 while content moves beneath it, or rising into place over footage as a clip settles, at about 80/84 weight 700. One short phrase, legible at every scroll position.

Two heading voices with fixed jobs: serif at 40-48px for chapters, sans at 30-38px flush left for features inside them, or the reverse. The reader learns the level from the voice alone. Never mix the two voices on one level.

Five left-aligned lines in a centred block, each opening with the same short word in bold accent sans at about 54px, followed by a serif phrase at the same size, about 67px line step. Repetition turns a stance into the strongest type moment on the page.

Mono uppercase label, 11-14px, weight 400, tracking 0.05-0.12em, mid-grey at about 5.5:1 contrast, 12-24px above the heading and flush with it. One label style per page, also used for footer heads and data keys, so mono always means metadata.

A 6-10px brand-derived marker (dot, square, hexagon, tag shape), 8-12px gap, then 11-14px uppercase mono or sans, tracking 0.05-0.1em, mid-grey. The marker is nearly the only chroma on the page. Place it top-left of the section, 16-40px above the heading.

Wrap or prefix the label with syntax such as square brackets, a double colon, double underscores or a numbered slash. Mono 11-14px caps, the token at about 40% ink and the word at 90%. Use one pattern everywhere, including nav and FAQ.

Mono caps 11-13px in a rectangle 22-30px tall, radius 0-4px, 1px outline or pale tinted fill, 8-12px side padding, colour following the section. Reuse the same tag for rails, states and diagram nodes, not just section titles, so it reads as one system.

Sentence case, no tracking, weight 500, 13-18px in the section accent, 8-24px above the H2. The largest version matches body size and reads as the heading's first line. No caps, pill or icon. The accent can shift by section, and flips on dark bands.

Sans or serif caps at 11-16px, weight 400-500, tracking 0.08-0.2em and up to 0.3em at 11px, warm grey or brand tint, 10-16px above a serif or light heading. Use on section intros only, never on every block.

Uppercase 10-14px with no added tracking, or at most 0.04em, black or 60% ink, no box or marker. Sits flush to the grid or sticks to a panel's top-left at 10-14px inset. A 2px size step from body can be the entire hierarchy.

A tag 24-36px tall, radius 4-8px or full, sentence case 13-16px weight 500. Pale tint fill with text in the same hue at 8-12% strength, or a 1px outline. About 24px above the heading. Hue identifies a product or section, never decoration.

One news link above the H1, 32-40px tall, full or zero radius, 13-16px label with arrow or chevron, 24-50px above the headline. Use one distinct device: a dark pill on a pale hero, one bright fill, or a hairline border. It must link to a real item.
One badge beside a plan name: 10-12px weight 500-600, 20-22px tall, full radius. Grey on grey keeps the recommended plan calm; a 10% tint of the only accent marks it once. No second badge on the row.

A short line anchors the label: a 22-56px 1px rule before or above, a 1x12px tick, or a full-width hairline with the label 16px below. Label 12-15px in ink or accent. For editorial meta, stretch a rule between byline and read time at 11px caps.

Tiny labels pinned to the page, not the heading: 10-12px numerals in the gutter, paired edge labels on one baseline, or mono captions in viewport corners 24-36px in. They replace dividers and eyebrows. Keep at least 10px and one ink step readable.

Two lines under or over media: name at 15-18px weight 400-500, detail at 12-15px in uppercase grey or mono, 4-8px apart. Keep sizes between 12 and 18px site-wide so text behaves as caption. Category colour can follow the project accent.

A label treated as an object: a paper tab with a small index inset 24px on the hero frame, a sticker tilted 3-5 degrees over a headline edge, a filled colour cell, or a script note. One per screen. Works when the brand has a physical world to draw on.

One to two sentences under the H1: 16-20px, weight 400, line-height 1.4-1.5, 60-85% of the heading's ink strength, 16-32px below, capped near 30em or 500-640px. H1 to sub is about 3:1. Balance centred lines so no word is stranded.

A lead sentence at 22-28px, line-height 1.25-1.4, with one to four words lit. Lit by colour, italic or underline, the sentence stays in full ink; lit by ink, the base drops to muted. Size never changes. The lit words alone should summarise the offer.
Lead in the display face, not the text face, 24-26px weight 400-500, line-height 1.35-1.4, 55-60% ink, capped at 600px, directly under the heading. Same family means hierarchy comes only from grey.

Name and promise set as one block at the same 28-32px size with line-height near 1.05: name in ink, promise in mid-grey, no gap between them. Body at 16px follows 6-8px below. For tiles, plan names and product cards.

No H1 above it: the lead itself takes the first screen, 30-45px, line-height 1.0-1.25, regular weight, 620-900px wide, flush left or centred. Works when the sentence is unusually good, and when imagery or a wordmark supplies the scale.
One dry line at 20-48px placed in the clear area of a full-bleed photograph, 24px inset, with one 16px underlined link 24-30px below, black or white by image tone. No button, no scrim.

One clause or glyph run recoloured inside a 28-36px sub: a soft two-colour fill with no hard stops, or per-word product colours. First and last words stay plain. One per section, never in the headline too. Everything around it stays monochrome.

The sub demonstrates the product: nouns become 34px outline pills with 1px border and a tinted hue inside a 20px sentence, line step about 44px, with one consistent pill style. The sentence replaces a feature list.

Long reading at 16-20px, line-height 1.5-1.65, 576-690px measure (about 70 characters), paragraph gap 20-30px. On dark use about 82% ink, near 13:1, and lift emphasis by weight and brightness. Links keep a 1px underline offset 3px. Subheads 20-24px with 48px above and 16px below.

Paragraph in muted ink, 16-21px, with proper nouns or key phrases lifted to full ink, with an optional +100 weight. Size never changes. Skimming only the dark words must give the argument. Two to five lifts per paragraph. A single accent or 1px underline is an acceptable alternative.

One paragraph, no separate title: a short bold phrase ending in a full stop, then regular text in the same ink on the same line. 16-18px, line-height 1.3-1.55, about 460px measure, 16-24px under the image. Or keep one weight and use two inks. Never both.

One size carries the whole page, anywhere from 12 to 35px, one weight. Hierarchy comes only from ink, position, case or italic: full ink for current, 50-60% for labels. Line-height 1.15-1.75. The grid does the structural work.

Serif carries all sentences at 15-21px, line-height 1.45-1.5; grotesque carries names, titles and labels at the same or a slightly smaller size. Measure 376-612px. No colour change needed, since family alone marks the role.

A short paragraph at 24-76px with display treatment: line-height 1.0-1.3, tracking to -0.03em, weight 300-400, 620-1100px wide. Once per page. Grey on dark at 24/33 stays quiet; serif italic at 45/45 becomes a voice.

Body or notes in mono or duospace, 12-16px, line-height 1.25-1.65, slightly open fit of +0.02em at 14-16px, measure under 690px. Use duospace for long text and true mono only for short notes and captions.

Within 17-46px prose, one clause per passage gets a physical mark: rough pale marker strokes per line overshooting about 10px, a rounded 3px outline around a word, inline pictograms, or an inline italic serif in a sans paragraph. The mark replaces bold.

Legal as typesetting: 12-15px, muted but readable, numbered notes with numerals hanging in the gutter, on the grid, tied to superscripts above, closed with a 1px rule. Alternatively three calm centred lines at 15/28, or two clamped lines with a fade and a Read more link.

Copy set as rows: label column and answer column on one baseline, 15/24, answers about 515px wide, 24px between groups. Or feature rows with a 14px check, about 30px pitch, wrapped lines hanging under the label, a 1px dotted underline marking a tooltip.

A narrow caption column 250-480px wide, 11-17px, line-height 1.25-1.55, beside large imagery or a title and set apart from the main flow. A scale jump of about 1:10 makes it read as a note. Keep it off busy images.

Pull quotes at about 18px, line-height 1.4-1.6, muted ink, with the opening quotation mark hung about 7px outside the column so the first letter aligns with the text above. Use a pseudo-element, since Chrome ignores hanging-punctuation.

Price 36-64px in the display sans, weight 500-700, tracking -0.02 to -0.05em; unit 14-16px on the same baseline in grey or mono, 4-10px gap. The word Custom takes the same size so columns align. Reserve a fixed line above for billing notes so all prices sit level.

Price at body size: 13-15px weight 600 rate, regular unit, grey add-on lines prefixed with a plus, in a stack about 90px tall. No oversized number; the plan name carries the weight. Hierarchy comes from weight and ink only.

One stat at 100-150px beside a quote, or up to three at 48-72px, weight 400-700, tracking -0.02 to -0.04em, proportional figures, caption 14-30px 4-12px below. Set units at half size in a lighter ink. Long counters take slight positive tracking. Accent at most one figure.

Stats as ledger rows: numeral 48-64px at left, 14px mono caps caption on the same baseline at right or below, 1px rule between rows. Serif numerals feel especially right. Reads as entries, not hero numbers.
Mono values at about 18px in ruled grid cells with 10px uppercase mono labels beneath in mid-grey, tabular figures. Values may count up on entry.

Oldstyle figures in running dates or in stats near 55px, so digits drop below the baseline and numbers feel literary. Confirm the face has them and set oldstyle-nums. Spell out months and use en dashes. Never in a table.

Digits roll vertically in a mask of one line height, stopping one by one, tabular-nums, at 14-140px. Trigger on entry, or tie to scroll or load. Render the real final value in the HTML so it survives no script and reduced motion.

Numerals as structure: a current index at 90-180px with a small denominator near 50px on the same baseline, a year pinned 35px from a bottom corner, or a 12px two-digit index before each row. They give the page a sense of place.

One rate on a plaque: a roughly 154px serif numeral with the percent and unit stacked beside it, on a light plaque inside a 20px-radius tile, with an illustration breaking the tile edge. One per page.

Close the page with the wordmark at 90-100% of container width, flush to the margins, weight 600-700, tracking -0.03 to -0.05em, cropped by the viewport bottom by 10-25% of cap height. Fit by measuring, not by guessing vw. One tone, mask or lit detail may be added.

Brand name fills the first screen edge to edge, 16-32px side margins, 130-300px tall, under or behind the nav. Let renders overlap it, or set it tone on tone near 1.1:1 as a watermark. The headline sits below at about a quarter of the size. Nav omits the logo.

A short line scaled to fill the container: 135-318px, line-height 0.75-0.85, tracking -0.04 to -0.05em, alone in a plain viewport, or two lines force-justified to the margins. Once per page, as a section break or sign-off. Fit the size by measuring.

Giant name at 250-360px behind a cut-out object or centred image that overlaps about a third of the letters. Letters run off an edge. Text stays flat while the object carries the shadow. The name must stay readable from what remains.

Headline at 45-80px with real objects in the line: photo chips, clock tiles, product cards, pills, about 1em tall, each a different shape, holding real content, radius 10-14px, 1px border, at most two per line. Raise line-height to 1.15-1.25 to clear them. The words alone must still be a sentence.

Letters as windows: clip a photo, gradient or live canvas through heavy condensed type at 200px or more with background-clip. A flat full stop keeps the word anchored. Keep the image simple enough that word shapes survive.
A chapter opener with a single year, word or set of initials at 300-920px wide, alone on a plain ground with only the nav remaining. Use between long sections. It may recolour per chapter.

Lines resolve on scroll: upcoming text blurred 6-10px at 30% opacity, sharpening as it reaches reading position. A static form steps each line dimmer, at 100%, 80%, then 60% ink, like baked poster text. Provide a fully legible state under reduced motion.

Single nouns swap to a transparent fill with a 1px stroke at the same size, inside solid lines, at most one per sentence, at 64px or above. Or a wall of outlined names with the active one filled. Use a face with simple contours.
A list at 52-64px replaces a grid: centred terms split by 5px squares, or client names stacked, about 86px row pitch. Hover fills a 4px-radius block behind a term. Inline badges can carry live data.
Letters built from something else: voxels, wind strands, a pixel grid, brush. Treat as artwork at section-break scale, one per site, with a live text alternative for readers and search.
Hand-drawn strokes on type: uneven ovals around a figure, pencil arrows into text, scrawled circles around names. Use SVG paths, drawn on entry. Annotation replaces section dividers.

Text lines each wrapped in a flat bright strip with 2px side padding, black text, bottom-left of a full-bleed slide. Use box-decoration-break: clone so padding repeats per line. It guarantees contrast over any photograph.

Typography as concept: the product name as a dictionary entry with phonetics and a small tag, or a forced-break monologue of caps at 40/44 in a 520px column. One idea, set exactly. The content must earn it.
